item.title: 8 takeaways from the Bears' stressful win over the Buccaneers
item.description: The victories seemed to be coming a little too easy for the Chicago Bears in recent weeks, so they made sure to put everyone through an extremely stressful one before heading off for their bye week. The Bears wrapped up their three-game prime-time tour with a home matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football and escaped with a 27-24 victory and improved to 7-2 on the season. Early on, however, it felt as if the game would be a blowout. Quarterback Caleb Williams quickly led two scoring drives to put the Bears up 14-0, with Tampa seemingly having no answers on either side of the ball. Everything was looking great, but then Williams began turning the ball over, something that is rare for him. Williams threw a career-high four interceptions on the day, and the Bears had five turnovers on the day. The offense couldn't muster any momentum, putting all the pressure on the Bears defense, which came through multiple times. The defense couldn't hold their ground forever, though. Eventually, those offensive miscues helped Tampa get back into the game as the Bears blew a 24-13 lead early in the fourth quarter to be tied 24-24 with just under two minutes to play. Fortunately, Williams responded by putting together one last scoring drive, complete with a big 38-yard completion to Colston Loveland to put the Bears in field goal range. Cairo Santos drilled a game-winning kick as everyone collectively exhaled. This will be one of the more memorable wins for all the wrong reasons, but it's still a win that keeps the Bears near the top of the playoff picture. Here are our takeaways from Sunday's stressful victory: 1. This is the reincarnation of 2006's Miracle in the Desert 20 years ago, Bears fans were treated to one of the most improbable and ugly wins in a special season. That, of course, was the "Miracle in the Desert" comeback win against the Arizona Cardinals, where the Bears committed six turnovers and needed big plays from the defense and special teams to get back in the game. And though this game may not have had the same comeback theatrics, it was every bit as gross and gritty to keep the winning streak alive. For nearly three full quarters, the offense didn't do much of anything and needed to rely on big plays by the defense to pick up the slack. It was ugly, and everything that could go wrong did go wrong. But the Bears never gave up and dug deep to get this victory. And great teams need to do that every once in a while. The Miracle in the Desert proved to everyone in the locker room that they have what it takes to win, no matter what happens. And that mindset helped propel them to Super Bowl XLI. Hopefully this will do the same, especially since it's the first time the Bears have won a game with a -3 turnover differential since then. We'll look back on this game with fond memories when the Bears are gunning for a title. 2. Caleb Williams had his worst game in 2 years This was a game we've quite literally never seen from Williams.

item.title: Jeffery Simmons’ hype post after Buccaneers thriller will have Bears fans ready to run through wall
item.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Jeffery Simmons’ hype post after Buccaneers thriller will have Bears fans ready to run through wall appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears have won four straight games and improved to 7-2 after a dramatic victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Their latest win also gave the team every reason to believe it can compete with the best in the NFL. Jeffery Simmons made that confidence clear after Sunday’s 27-24 thriller. The defensive tackle took to his X, formerly Twitter, account and shared a powerful message embracing his new team and its growing momentum. Simmons joined Chicago in a blockbuster trade with the Tennessee Titans in late October. The Bears sent two first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round selection to Tennessee for the four-time Pro Bowler and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The veteran has quickly embraced his new surroundings, including choosing No. 99 for what he called a fresh chapter in his career. Montez Sweat offered to give up No. 98, the number Simmons wore in Tennessee, but the defensive tackle wanted something different. After the Buccaneers game, Simmons backed Caleb Williams despite the quarterback throwing four interceptions. He credited Williams for delivering when Chicago needed a late scoring drive. “One thing I told Caleb is, we got his back,” Simmons said. “And just like at the end of the game when we really needed to get down in field goal range, he did his part.” “It’s our job to go out there and just draw the line, and that’s what we’re going to continue to do. We have his back, and once we put a complete game together, good luck,” he added. Chicago has not played a complete game yet, but its recent results have strengthened its position. With Simmons leading the defensive front and the offense finding ways to deliver late, the Bears have plenty of reasons to believe their best football could still be ahead. Related: Caleb Williams’ defiant declaration after 4-interception nightmare for Bears highlights gunslinger mentality Related: Wacky Bears-Buccaneers game ended 2 decades-old NFL streaks

item.title: Vote for the South Shore High School Male Athlete of the Week
item.description: Pembroke High soccer player Dylan Baldwin has been voted the South Shore High School Male Athlete of the Week . Baldwin received more than 760 votes (55 percent of the total votes cast) to earn the honor. He had a hat trick and 2 assists in a 9-1 win over North Quincy that clinched the Titans' sixth consecutive Patriot League Fisher Division crown. Baldwin also had an assist in a 3-0 win over Scituate. Hanover High soccer player Brenton Long was second with more than 460 votes (33 percent of the total). And this week's candidates are ... The poll The candidates Chase Denison, Archbishop Williams boys soccer Denison scored a pair of late goals as the playoff-bound Bishops beat Monomoy, 2-1, in their regular-season finale. Lucas Heald, Duxbury boys soccer Heald had a hat trick and an assist as the Dragons beat Whitman-Hanson, 6-1, in their regular-season finale. He scored again in a 3-1 victory over Middleboro in the preliminary round of the Division 2 playoffs. Tommy McAuliffe, Pembroke boys soccer McAuliffe had a hat trick as the playoff-bound Titans beat Nauset, 4-1, in their regular-season finale. D.J. Neto, Quincy boys cross country Neto finished 10th overall at the MSTCA Frank Mooney Coaches Invitational Large-School senior race, covering the 5K course at Wrentham Development Center in 16:52. Cooper Nelson, North Quincy boys cross country Nelson finished 12th overall at the MSTCA Frank Mooney Coaches Invitational Large-School junior race, covering the 5K course at Wrentham Development Center in 17:15. Terrance McGhee, BC High cross country McGhee finished fourth overall at the MSTCA Frank Mooney Coaches Invitational Large-School sophomore race, covering the 5K course at Wrentham Development Center in 16:52. J.P. Newman, South Shore Tech boys cross country Newsom finished 26th overall at the MSTCA Frank Mooney Coaches Invitational Small School/Medium School junior/senior race, covering the 5K course at Wrentham Development Center in 17:10. Votes are unlimited. Voting closes on Monday, Nov. 16 at noon. Emailed votes will not be counted. Send future nominations to cmcdaniel@wickedlocal.com. Our player of the week stories are meant as a way to highlight local high school athletes in the area. Making the list is an achievement in itself. Congratulations to all our athlete s. item.title: Harry Kane left out of FIFPRO World 11 team as Messi returns
item.description: Harry Kane left out of FIFPRO World 11 team as Messi returns Lionel Messi has extended his record number of FIFPRO World 11 appearances to 18, while Lucy Bronze has set a new women’s record after being selected for the ninth time. More than 26,000 professional footballers from 75 countries voted for the 2026 men’s and women’s teams. Messi returns to the team for the first time since 2023 and is joined in the men’s XI by the likes of Erling Haaland, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Though there is no place for Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane. Yamal has also made history by becoming the first player to earn two World 11 selections before turning 20. Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is selected after helping Spain win the 2026 World Cup, with compatriots Pau Cubarsi and Rodri also included. Jude Bellingham is the only English player in the men’s side, while Paris Saint-Germain trio Achraf Hakimi, Nuno Mendes and Vitinha are all recognised. In the women’s team, Bronze makes a record ninth appearance and is one of five England players selected. Chelsea goalkeeper Hannah Hampton, Manchester City defender Alex Greenwood, Manchester United midfielder Ella Toone and Arsenal striker Alessia Russo also make the XI. Barbra Banda is the only player in the women’s team from outside England or Spain, with the Zambia forward earning her third selection. 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World 11 Goalkeeper: David Raya (Arsenal, Spain) Defenders: Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona, Spain), Achraf Hakimi (Paris Saint-Germain, Morocco), Nuno Mendes (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Midfielders: Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid, England), Rodri (Manchester City/Barcelona, Spain), Vitinha (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Forwards: Erling Haaland (Manchester City, Norway), Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid, France), Lionel Messi (Inter Miami, Argentina), Lamine Yamal (Barcelona, Spain) 2026 FIFPRO Women’s World 11 Goalkeeper: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea, England) Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea, England), Alex Greenwood (Manchester City, England), Mapi Leon (Barcelona/London City Lionesses, Spain), Irene Paredes (Barcelona, Spain) Midfielders: Aitana Bonmati (Barcelona, Spain), Alexia Putellas (Barcelona/London City Lionesses, Spain), Ella Toone (Manchester United, England) Forwards: Barbra Banda (Orlando Pride, Zambia), Claudia Pina (Barcelona, Spain), Alessia Russo (Arsenal, England) The men’s voting was based on performances between August 4, 2025 and July 19, 2026, while the women’s voting period ran until August 16. Players selected the three footballers they believed had performed best in each position, with the highest-ranked players forming the final World 11.

item.title: Broncos’ Jonah Coleman’s insane 8-week body transformation highlighted on CBS broadcast
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Broncos’ Jonah Coleman’s insane 8-week body transformation highlighted on CBS broadcast appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Denver Broncos rookie running back Jonah Coleman is turning heads for more than just his performances on the field. The young ball carrier recently caught viewers’ attention after CBS showcased his remarkable physical transformation , revealing how much his physique changed in just eight weeks. According to a graphic featured during CBS’ broadcast and reshared by NFL insider Jordan Schultz on X, Coleman went from 236 pounds at 16.8% body fat to 222 pounds at 14.2% in just two months. The before-and-after images showed a noticeably leaner and more defined athlete, prompting plenty of reactions from football fans. CBS just showed this graphic that #Broncos RB Jonah Coleman did this in 8 weeks?!!? pic.twitter.com/yAhRntFkhG — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 8, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The dramatic change quickly sparked reactions on social media, with fans joking about how much Coleman had changed in such a short period. One fan even wrote, “You have been selected for a random drug test per the NFL” 😂, before adding the hashtag #beast. The comment reflected the disbelief surrounding the rookie’s impressive physical transformation. The transformation originally took place during Coleman’s time at the University of Washington in March 2025, well before Denver selected him in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft . The 5-foot-8 running back’s physical changes reportedly helped him develop better agility, explosiveness, and movement while maintaining his strength. His conditioning has also translated into encouraging production in Denver. Coleman delivered 104 scrimmage yards and a rushing touchdown against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 8, contributing to the Broncos’ recent success , before following it up with another touchdown against Carolina. He finished Sunday’s contest with 88 total yards, giving Denver another reliable option in its backfield.” With his workload growing, the rookie will have another opportunity to establish himself as an important piece of Denver’s offense. item.title: Fantasy football waiver wire: Which unheralded RB will save your season?
item.description: The final five weeks of the fake football regular season have descended on us like creeping 5 p.m. darkness after Daylight Savings Time. Week 9 was filled with unexpected fantasy heroes who may, or may not, be able to stand out as trusted contributors and bail your fantasy team out of purgatory and into the postseason. We were treated to heartwarming stories like “Tank Dell is back” and more confusing ones like “Audric Estime and Kaleb Johnson were leading rushers for winning teams.” Weird weeks deserve weird fantasy coverage. So, instead of our typical add/drop analysis for a couple unexpected studs, we’re going to break down four running backs who stood out and who you should prioritize with a dwindling pool of free agent cash. Then, we’ll do the same for this week's top wideouts in another post (and video). I'm joined by fantasy expert and Rhode Island Scumbag Mike "Yaj" Boyajian to break down the players who shined in Week 9 and figure out if they’ll be able to keep it up over the back half of the 2026 NFL season. The rules? There's pretty much only one; players have to be 40 percent owned or less in Yahoo! fantasy football leagues. We've got a handful of backs who can spark a bidding war on your waiver wire this week. Let's see if we can help prioritize those bids. Rank the running backs who played their way off the waiver wire: Audric Estime, Kaleb Johnson, Seth McGowan and Kaelon Black Christian : 1. Audric Estime, New Orleans Saints . Estime is a mess. Good news! So are the rest of the Saints. Travis Etienne has yet to have his practice window activated even though he’s eligible to return from injured reserve. Alvin Kamara has posted negative rush yards over expected (RYOE) for the fifth straight season and his -1.2 RYOE per rush is second worst in the NFL behind only MarShawn Lloyd . In third place on that ranking of shame is Kendre Miller, who isn’t even on the roster anymore. Estime didn’t even start this season with New Orleans. But he was efficient in small doses there last year. His 19 RYOE in Week 9 was third-best among all tailbacks . He has, at the moment, the brightest combination of efficiency and opportunity. 2. Seth McGowan, Indianapolis Colts . Jonathan Taylor said goodbye to Colts fans in his postgame scrum. McGowan got a goal line carry early and eventually got six carries to Taylor’s 13. His 36-yard run was the second-longest play from scrimmage Indianapolis had Sunday. Even if Taylor isn’t traded – and publishing this the morning of the trade deadline could make us look very, very dumb very, very quickly – he should get some meaningful opportunities going forward for a team weighing its young talent. 3. Kaelon Black, San Francisco 49ers . Black had fewer carries and more rushing yards than Christian McCaffrey in Week 9, but 40 of his 70 yards came in the fourth quarter of a 35-17 game. item.title: Tinubu’s projects, security efforts boosting South-East economy — Shettima
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has said the administration of President Bola Tinubu is driving economic growth and improving security in the South-East through investments in road infrastructure, agriculture, renewable energy, housing and human capital development. Shettima said the Federal Government’s interventions in Ebonyi State and the wider South-East were aimed at improving regional connectivity, strengthening food security, expanding economic opportunities and addressing longstanding development challenges. The Vice-President spoke on Monday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, where he urged residents to renew Tinubu’s mandate in the 2027 general elections. He said the administration had demonstrated its commitment to Ebonyi through major infrastructure projects, federal appointments and policies designed to improve citizens’ welfare. “This campaign has been a season of triumph. We have triumphed over the falsehoods of our opponents. We have triumphed over those who mistook the limits of their imagination for the limits of our reach. “We have never turned our backs on you. We have answered your support with projects and His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has honoured Ebonyi through distinguished appointments and projects across the state,” he said. Shettima described public office as a responsibility to deliver measurable improvements in the lives of citizens, adding that the administration was seeking another mandate to consolidate its development programmes. “If any state can speak with confidence about the dividends of democracy, it is Ebonyi. You have stood by us. You have assured us that a mandate is a debt of honour, repayable only through service. Yet democracy demands the humility of asking again. “We have returned to seek the renewal of your mandate, to serve you, to defend you, and to stand by you,” he said. Highlighting federal infrastructure investments, the Vice-President listed the Calabar–Ebonyi–Benue–Kogi–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway as one of the major projects expected to strengthen trade and economic integration between the South-East, North-Central and other parts of the country. He also mentioned the Ndibe Bridge, which is designed to connect Ebonyi with Cross River State, as well as ongoing work on the Enugu–Abakaliki–Ogoja Expressway and the Okposi–Ohaozara–Ukawu–Cross River road. According to him, the projects will ease the movement of agricultural produce, manufactured goods and other commodities while reducing transportation challenges for businesses and communities. On agriculture, Shettima described Ebonyi as an important contributor to Nigeria’s food security, particularly in rice and cassava production. He said the Federal Government was supporting farmers through fertiliser distribution, interest-free FarmerMoni assistance and other agricultural development programmes. item.title: What channel is Penn State football vs Minnesota? Time, TV, streaming
item.description: Finally, Penn State football appears to be getting on a of a roll again. Coach Matt Campbell and his Nittany Lions have won consecutive games for the first time since mid-September and now will prepare for their last marquee home game of the season. The Lions (5-4, 2-4 Big Ten) will face the Minnesota Golden Gophers in prime time on Saturday, Nov. 14, in Beaver Stadium. The Gophers, also 5-4, are coming off tough losses against top-five Indiana and UCLA but have played well under coach PJ Fleck. Penn State will continue to build off premium efforts from quarterback Rocco Becht, running back Carson Hansen and receiver Chase Sowell on offense and from All-America-trending linebacker Tony Rojas and some splendid cornerback work on defense. The Gophers' top player? That may well be defensive end Anthony Smith, the All-Big Ten performer who was a three-sport star at Shippensburg High. Here's how to watch Penn State's Big Ten game vs. Minnesota, including time, TV schedule, streaming info, game odds and more. When is Penn State football vs Minnesota? Kickoff between Penn State (4-4, 2-4 Big Ten) and Minnesota (5-4, 3-3) is scheduled for 7 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 14, in Beaver Stadium. What TV channel is Penn State vs Minnesota on? item.title: Giants get great news on Cam Skattebo as fan favorite RB should be ‘full go’ in Week 10
item.description: Giants get great news on Cam Skattebo as fan favorite RB should be ‘full go’ in Week 10 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Giants beat the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 9, and they did so without their top two running backs. Cam Skattebo was out due to a hamstring injury, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on injured reserve. Devin Singletary led the backfield, but it wasn't a very productive day on the ground. Getting Skattebo back as soon as possible is a must for this Giants' offense to function. They could trade for an RB as well, but Skattebo returning is the easiest way to improve. Fortunately, John Harbaugh told reporters, including Pat Leonard of NY Daily News Sports , that Skattebo should be a "full go" for the team in Week 10 when they face the Washington Commanders on Thursday Night Football. Giants expecting to get Cam Skattebo back for TNF "John Harbaugh says Cam Skattebo (hamstring) should be 'full go' Thursday night vs. the Washington Commanders," Leonard reports. "He was close to being able to play vs. the Eagles, but they were careful with him." This is a very encouraging update for the Giants on their fan favorite running back. While Skattebo didn't suit up in Week 9, he reportedly was close to playing. But with the Eagles being one of the worst teams in the NFL since Jalen Hurts was lost for the season, it made sense for the Giants to give Skattebo an extra week of rest. They had the ability to win without him, and did. MORE : Eagles’ Braden Mann boots punt not seen in over 20 years For Week 10, however, facing the Commanders and Jayden Daniels, having a good ground game will be huge. They could trade for Jonathan Taylor or another running back before the trade deadline, but they're set to get Skattebo back this week. Despite the fact that the Giants are playing the Commanders on Thursday Night Football, a short week, Skattebo is set to return for New York, providing a big boost to the offense. This is some great news for the Giants, as relying on the backfield they trotted out in Philadelphia is a recipe for disaster against more competitive teams. Skattebo is set to return and be a "full go" for the Giants on Thursday Night Football. It's some great news for the Giants, as they try to get to 6-2-1 and further separate themselves from the pack in the NFC East race. item.title: Dan Campbell Has Complicated Decision to Make Before Germany Game
item.description: The Detroit Lions improved to 6-2 with Sunday’s 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins, but head coach Dan Campbell now has an interesting decision to make regarding his offensive line. And based on what happened in Miami, it might be a decision that is easier to make on paper than in the locker room. Christian Mahogany was surprisingly benched for violating team rules, opening the door for second-year offensive lineman Miles Frazier to make his first NFL start at left guard. Unfortunately for Detroit, the results weren’t exactly encouraging. Campbell has built his program around accountability, and that’s not something he should abandon. However, with the Lions preparing for another important matchup against the New England Patriots, the question becomes whether Mahogany has already served his punishment or whether Campbell intends to make a longer-term change. Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions offensive lineman Christian Mahogany (73) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Miles Frazier’s Performance Raises Questions for Detroit Lions According to Lions Wire’s report on Frazier’s first start , the young offensive lineman received a disappointing 31.9 overall offensive grade from Pro Football Focus. His 48.8 pass-blocking grade and team-worst 37.8 run-blocking grade certainly won’t help his argument for remaining in the starting lineup. Frazier played all 59 offensive snaps against Miami, while Mahogany played exclusively on special teams. The Lions also struggled offensively, producing a season-low 270 total yards while Jared Goff was sacked three times. Of course, it would be unfair to blame Detroit’s offensive struggles entirely on Frazier. The offensive line had multiple issues, and Frazier did appear to settle down as the game progressed. However, the numbers make one thing clear: Frazier did not do enough in his first start to make the decision at left guard an obvious one. Dan Campbell Must Balance Discipline With Winning Following Sunday’s victory, Campbell made it clear that Mahogany’s benching was related to team rules rather than simply his performance on the field. The Lions have not publicly revealed what rule Mahogany violated, so judging the severity of the punishment would be premature. Speaking during his postgame press conference , Campbell explained his decision: “Well, that was just, that was team rules, Mahogany. It was really that simple. Miles deserved his opportunity, and he got it. And it doesn’t mean it stays that way, but that was the way it was going to be today.” That final sentence is particularly important because Campbell clearly left the door open for Mahogany to return. Considering Mahogany entered the game ranked among Pro Football Focus’ top 10 qualifying guards, there is a strong football argument for putting him back on the field. item.title: ‘There was some deli meat given out’: Tom Brady takes jab at Drake Maye
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Tom Brady returned to Foxboro this weekend for Rob Gronkowski’s New England Patriots Hall of Fame induction Saturday and Sunday’s game between the Pats and the Green Bay Packers. The former event went swimmingly for New England fans; the latter less so. Led by Jordan Love’s 372 passing yards and four total touchdowns, the Packers routed the Patriots 45-27. Drake Maye, New England’s third-year quarterback, had his share of struggles, tossing three critical interceptions. After the game, Brady the broadcaster had some fun at Maye’s expense during FOX’s postgame interviews. Drake throwing ‘deli meat’ Speaking with Green Bay Packers safety Evan Williams (five tackles, one interception), Brady noted that Maye was being generous with his passes throughout the game. “Xavier [McKinney] had two picks, you had one on the sideline. There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today,” Brady said . “I’m not gonna say that,” Williams responded, laughing, “but he was giving us some gifts for sure.” “There was a few out there, and you made him pay,” Brady added. Tom Brady took a dig at Drake Maye while interviewing #Packers S Evan Williams: “There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today.” ( @NFLonFOX) https://t.co/qp4SfQj1qP — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 9, 2026 If you’re unfamiliar, Brady’s “deli meat” reference is a nod to Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake, who said last week that struggling Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was “throwing deli meat out there” in a loss to the Rams. Lake later apologized to Herbert via text message, claiming he wasn’t trying to be “disrespectful.” Back to Brady We’re guessing Brady wasn’t trying to be cruel toward Maye with his postgame barb, even if his assessment was harsh (though not unfair). After throwing only four touchdowns and seven interceptions in his first four games, Maye tossed 11 TDs and only one pick his next four before Sunday’s ugly showing. “We haven’t had a clean, a turnover-free game yet. It’s, starting with me, it’s one of the biggest differences between winning and losing football games,” Maye said after yesterday’s loss. “I’d say, put our defense in a bad spot in the first, the first drive, and just gave them the football and had some other chances down the field and got to see in front. I got to see in front. I feel like I was just a little late sometimes. I feel like we got into a throwing game, and that’s partly because of what we did offensively, and then we didn’t really get to build off the run game, and I think we just got to start the game, and me specifically, start better.” New England is back in action this Sunday when they take on the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany. The post ‘There was some deli meat given out’: Tom Brady takes jab at Drake Maye appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: PANDEF urges police, DSS to probe political violence in South-South
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA: The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has called on the Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to investigate recent incidents of political violence in Warri and Asaba, Delta State, and Calabar, Cross River State, and prosecute those responsible. The apex socio-political organisation of the South-South region also called for an immediate end to political violence, intimidation and thuggery, warning that such activities were alien to the values and traditions of peaceful coexistence in the region. PANDEF made the call in a statement issued on Monday and signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali. The organisation expressed concern over the incidents, particularly the reported loss of life in Asaba, and described the violence as a threat to peaceful coexistence in the Niger Delta. It specifically cited incidents in the Warri/Effurun axis on September 18, 2026; Calabar on November 4; and Asaba on November 7, 2026. The statement read: “The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) notes with very serious concern and strongly condemns the disturbing incidents of political violence recorded around our region. Most worrisome are the sad events which occurred in the Warri/Effurun axis on Friday, 18th September 2026; in Calabar on Wednesday, 4th November, 2026 and most recently, the incident in Asaba on Saturday, 7th November 2026 in which a life was lost! “Indeed, as the mother body of the peoples of the region, PANDEF views these developments as a sacrilege to our peaceful co-existence in the Niger Delta and strongly condemns them.” Igali said peaceful coexistence, tolerance and political forbearance were values inherited from the region’s founding fathers and must be preserved. He urged political leaders, party supporters and other stakeholders to demonstrate maturity and embrace sportsmanship in resolving political disagreements. The forum also warned political leaders against inflammatory rhetoric, provocation and actions capable of triggering violence, stressing that they had a responsibility to guide their followers. PANDEF particularly appealed to youths in the Niger Delta not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence, intimidation or thuggery. It urged young people to channel their energy towards peaceful and constructive political participation rather than serving the interests of selfish political actors. “PANDEF hereby makes a special appeal to the youths of the Niger Delta not to allow themselves to be used as cannon fodders, instruments of political violence, thuggery or intimidation,” the statement added. The organisation further advised political parties to hold rallies and large gatherings in properly secured venues, with adequate security arrangements, particularly during movement to and from event locations. It said such measures would improve crowd control, minimise the risk of clashes and protect participants. PANDEF called on all stakehold

item.title: Seahawks vs. Raiders odds: Opening lines for Week 10 matchup
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks, as expected, are a favorite to win versus the Las Vegas Raiders and former Seahawks offensive coordinator and current Raiders head coach, Klint Kubiak. Per the current lines at FanDuel Sportsbook , Seattle is a 3.5-point favorite (-105) . The Seahawks’ money line is – 180, while the Raisers’ sits at + 154. The game total is set at 43.5 points . The Seahawks have outscored their opponents by 4.4 points so far this season and are 5-4. Meanwhile, the Raiders margin of victory is -3.4. Drew Lock is a question mark this game, but he believes he will play . Sam Darnold doesn’t sound likely to return until after the bye week. Per DVOA , the Raiders are the 31st ranked defense and the 15th ranked offense. Meanwhile, the Seahawks are the second-ranked defense and the 19th ranked offense. After a 3-0 start, the Raiders are 4-5 and coming off a devastating 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, while the 5-4 Seahawks held the Arizona Cardinals to three points in a two-touchdown victory. Whether it is Drew Lock at the helm, or Jalen Milroe, with more players coming back from injury (hopefully), the Seahawks should be able to cover and win this game.

item.title: TD Cowen Gives Stablecoin Yield Ban 10% Odds as Banks Plan Push in Democrat-Led Congress
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine TD Cowen Gives Stablecoin Yield Ban 10% Odds as Banks Plan Push in Democrat-Led Congress Banks will try again to stop crypto platforms from paying yield on stablecoin balances, but TD Cowen’s Washington analyst Jaret Seiberg puts only a 10% chance on Congress enacting such a ban over the next two years, he wrote in a Monday policy note shared with Bitcoin Magazine and clients. The issue is whether exchanges and other platforms can offer yield or rewards to investors who keep dollar-pegged stablecoins on their platforms. Seiberg views action as unlikely, though he sees a “narrow path” for a ban. His rationale is procedural as much as political: it may be easier to find 60 Senate votes on stablecoin yield alone than on the broader crypto market structure bill, which failed a cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and which he already called effectively dead for this Congress after the Democratic midterm sweep. A ban, he wrote, would benefit banks. He expects them to renew the push in the next Congress on the theory that Democratic wins open a path. Why Seiberg still sees a path That path rests on a shift in the Senate. Key crypto advocates retired or lost, while skeptics are being elevated. Sen. Elizabeth Warren is likely to chair the Banking Committee, and Sen. Sherrod Brown, a longtime critic of the industry, regained his Ohio seat after crypto-backed spending of about $64 million failed to stop him, Seiberg wrote before the votes were counted. It is not his base case. Crypto politics are “complex,” he wrote, which is why the probability starts at 10%. Some Democrats will resist treating stablecoin yield outside a broader package. Seiberg again sees no path for the Clarity Act, arguing Democrats will insist on ethics and investor-protection provisions President Trump would reject. That split, he wrote, makes Democrats unlikely to unite behind a yield-only bill. Democrats are not united on the substance either. Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, a lead Democrat on crypto policy, has backed paying rewards for using stablecoins rather than for passively holding them, a distinction that shaped the Tillis-Alsobrooks compromise text during Clarity talks. There is also a perception problem. Congress would be asked to stop voters from earning a return on stablecoin holdings even though they can earn one on savings accounts and money market funds. Seiberg questions whether Democratic leaders want a vote that could be framed as taking money from retail investors. What GENIUS already banned, and what it left open The fight is leftover business from the GENIUS Act, which President Trump signed on July 18, 2025, as Public Law 119-27. The statute bars permitted and foreign payment stablecoin issuers from paying “any form of interest or yield” solely for holding, using or retaining a payment stablecoin. It does not explicitly cover exchanges and other intermediaries. That gap is what banks call the loophole. The American Bankers Association and state bankers asso

item.title: Nvidia’s board needs to do some succession planning – sharpish | Nils Pratley
item.description: The chipmaker faces business risks and political scrutiny due to its over-reliance on founder and CEO Jensen Huang Why is Nvidia’s Jensen Huang at the centre of a US-China row? Too big – and too well-connected – to sack? One doesn’t have to be overly cynical to think Jensen Huang, the Nvidia boss, starts with one huge advantage as the chipmaker’s board starts its independent investigation into the alleged honeytrap spy scandal . The world of US big tech is not, to put it mildly, strong on checks and balances on a founder’s power. Huang does not enjoy the supercharged voting rights that are par for the course elsewhere – his shareholding is a plain vanilla 3.6%. On the other hand, Nvidia’s board does not appear to have spent much time worrying about succession planning and “key person risk” or other standard concerns of corporate governance wonks outside the US. item.title: No room for Kane! Messi back in FIFPRO XI as Yamal breaks teenage record
item.description: Inter Miami CF v Charlotte FC - Getty Images Sport The 2026 FIFPRO Men's World 11 has been officially announced, featuring a mix of legendary veterans and record-breaking youngsters. However, the selection has sparked debate following the high-profile exclusion of Harry Kane, despite the England striker holding the 2026 Ballon d'Or. Messi returns as Yamal makes history Lionel Messi has secured his place in the FIFPRO Men's World 11 once again, marking a triumphant return to the elite lineup for the first time since 2023. His comeback follows a stellar international campaign where he scored eight goals to lead Argentina to the World Cup final, which they narrowly lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time. Joining him in the history books is Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal, who continues to shatter expectations . The Spanish international has become the first player ever to be selected for the World 11 twice before reaching the age of 20. He is one of four Spanish players included in this season's lineup, alongside David Raya, Pau Cubarsi, and Rodri Hernandez. Shock omission for Harry Kane The biggest talking point of the announcement is undoubtedly the absence of Kane. Despite the England captain being the reigning Ballon d'Or winner , he failed to garner enough votes from his fellow professionals to make the final cut. Kane's exclusion highlights the intense competition for attacking spots, with voters clearly favouring a standout frontline. Erling Haaland secured his place after finishing as the Premier League top scorer last season with 27 goals, while also scoring seven times to lead Norway to their first-ever World Cup quarter-final. Alongside him, Kylian Mbappe earned his spot after bagging 10 goals to finish as the World Cup top scorer, officially becoming the tournament's all-time leading goalscorer. Ligue 1 and PSG dominance Paris Saint-Germain enjoyed a strong showing in the final XI, with the French champions boasting three representatives in the squad following their back-to-back Champions League titles. The defensive unit features Moroccan star Achraf Hakimi and Portuguese left-back Nuno Mendes, alongside midfielder Vitinha, all rewarded for their pivotal roles in the club's European success. The lineup was selected following a vote by 19,806 professional footballers across 73 countries. Eligible players were evaluated on their performances between August 4, 2025, and July 19, 2026, provided they featured in at least 30 official matches during that period. The complete 2026 FIFPro World 11 The complete 2026 FIFPro World 11 lineup features Raya in goal, behind a backline of Hakimi, Cubarsi, and Mendes. The midfield trio consists of Rodri, Vitinha, and Jude Bellingham, while Messi, Yamal, Mbappe, and Haaland form a formidable frontline. The 2026 FIFPRO Men’s #World11 ✨ Decided exclusively by 19,806 professional men’s footballers worldwide. By the players, for the players 🏆 pic.twitter.com/MnHEMHxtf1 — FIFPRO (@FIFPRO) November 9, 2026

item.description: NBA superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo has responded to criticism from his former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers, dismissing the comments and suggesting they were driven by bitterness. I gotta focus on my team and what I gotta do…goddamn that’s crazy — never let bitterness or pettiness get in front of your goals and dreams…that’s insane you gotta go ask him why he said what he said— not me.” (@eric_nehm) — The HEAT Realm (@WadexFlash) November 9, 2026 The two-time MVP also described Rivers’ comments as “insane” and appeared surprised by the criticism from someone he worked closely with for more than two years. item.title: What Does T.J. Paganetti Firing Actually Fix for the Saints?
item.description: After recording 18 rushing yards on 17 carries against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the New Orleans Saints entered the bye week searching for answers to their struggling run game. On Nov. 2, the Saints announced the firing of run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti and tasked offensive line coach Brendan Nugent with leading the run game. Nugent already played a significant role in preparing the rushing attack. What does Paganetti’s firing fix for the Saints going forward? From Super Bowl Champ To Unemployed From 2023 to 2024 in Philadelphia, Paganetti was the run game specialist. In 2024, the Eagles ranked second in rushing with 3,048 yards . Philadelphia went on to win Super Bowl LIX and averaged 204.5 rushing yards across their four playoff games. After winning the Super Bowl with Moore, the Saints hired him as their run game coordinator. In 2025, New Orleans finished 28th in rushing yards per game and 31st in yards per carry. In his seven games as coordinator in 2026 , the Saints remained 28th in rushing yards per game and ranked 30th in yards per carry, with their average dropping from 3.7 to 3.5. After the firing, Paganetti’s brother Ryan claimed in a now-deleted X post that Paganetti’s role was more of a support role rather than installing and implementing run techniques. Interesting nugget from Ryan Paganetti “Run Game Coordinator title in New Orleans was not what was expected, really was just a smaller support role as Kellen/Nugent designed, installed, and taught the run techniques. “ https://t.co/uF4BMboPj4 — Brenden Ertle (@BrendenErtle) November 2, 2026 Kellen Moore ‘s explanation for the firing was, “I just felt like coming out of the bye week, we needed to make adjustments (in) workflow.” Moore also confirmed that offensive line coach Brendan Nugent would lead the weekly run structure, while running backs coach Joel Thomas continued contributing to situational planning. However, Nugent was already responsible for some of the team’s run-game installations, which Moore said would remain unchanged. With Nugent taking on more responsibility, it’s important to look at how he’s done as an offensive line coach. A History of Rushing Troubles Brendan Nugent has served as offensive line coach for the Saints and the Chargers. His units have struggled to rank among the NFL’s best according to Pro Football Focus (PFF). In his first season leading the line in 2021, the Saints finished 18th in PFF’s rankings. In his first season with the Chargers in 2022, Los Angeles ranked 30th in rushing yards per game and yards per carry, averaging 89.6 rushing yards per game and 3.8 yards per attempt. In 2023, the Chargers improved to 25th , averaging 96.6 yards per game. Their yards per attempt, however, remained the same at 3.8. That season also marked the first time Nugent worked under Kellen Moore, then Los Angeles’ offensive coordinator. item.title: Fani-Kayode urges South Africa to replace xenophobia with Pan-Africanism
item.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has called on South Africa to embrace Pan-Africanism and reject xenophobic sentiments that have fuelled attacks on Nigerians and other African nationals in the country. Fani-Kayode made the call on Saturday while speaking at the inaugural Nigerian Fair held at the Nigerian Consulate in Johannesburg. He recalled Nigeria’s contributions, alongside other African countries, to the struggle against apartheid in South Africa, stressing that the liberation movement was a collective African effort. “It wasn’t a black South African struggle. It was a struggle that every nation in Africa led primarily by the frontline states and Nigeria, and every decent civilized nation in the world supported,” he said. The high commissioner urged South Africans not to forget the sacrifices made by Nigeria and other African countries towards ending apartheid. He said Nigeria and the rest of Africa had a stake in South Africa’s development because of their contributions to the country’s liberation. Fani-Kayode described xenophobic attacks as a retrogressive sentiment, urging African countries to strengthen solidarity and cooperation. “We must understand that the world is coming together as one, and we must stand together as one,” he said. He claimed that Nigeria contributed no less than $61 billion to the anti-apartheid struggle between 1960 and 1994, adding that the country also deployed troops to frontline states in support of the campaign against the apartheid regime. He cited the introduction of the “Mandela Tax”, through which Nigerian civil servants contributed financially to the struggle, as one of the country’s solidarity measures. “Nigeria did so much. Mandela tax — we imposed a tax on our own civil servants during the course of the struggle, and that money was channelled to the ANC,” he said. He added that Nigerian schoolchildren also contributed their lunch money to support the struggle, while the country consistently advocated South Africa’s liberation at the United Nations and other international platforms. Fani-Kayode called for stronger ties between Nigeria and South Africa, urging both countries to build bridges of friendship, fraternity and mutual respect. He described perpetrators of xenophobic attacks as a minority driven by what he called Afrophobia and xenophobia. The high commissioner said Nigeria must continue to promote African unity and avoid actions that could further strain relations between the two countries. He also said Nigeria would not sever its economic ties with South Africa despite calls by some Nigerians for such a move, although he acknowledged that patience was wearing thin within the corridors of power. Fani-Kayode assured Nigerians living in South Africa that the Federal Government would continue to take steps to protect their interests and ensure their welfare. item.title: Heisman Trophy watch: 5 leading college football candidates entering Week 11
item.description: This year’s Heisman race is getting complicated because the most high-profile players’ teams keep losing. Fernando Mendoza won on an undefeated Indiana team last year, but recent history has shown the Heisman committee’s willingness to pick players on flawed teams. Travis Hunter , Jayden Daniels and Caleb Williams all won on teams that failed to compete for a National Championship. The two remaining unbeaten teams are the UCLA Bruins and Utah Utes. Only one of those teams has someone worthy of Heisman consideration right now and that’s a longshot. Here is this week’s Heisman watch list. item.title: When is the NFL trade deadline? See which Eagles might get traded
item.description: For the first time in years, the Philadelphia Eagles find themselves in a rare position as likely sellers as the NFL trade deadline nears. In what experts predicted would be a possible Super Bowl run and at the very least a third straight NFC East Division title, the Birds are currently at the bottom of the division and with one of the worst records in the league at 2-7. Much of the blame can be blamed on injuries up and down the roster with the main blow coming after quarterback Jalen Hurts was ruled out for the season due to blood clots in his lungs. Losing future Hall of Fame right tackle Lane Johnson to retirement hurt just as much. But inconsistent play calling from both sides of the ball haven't helped either as new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion's system has been a dud halfway through the season. New offensive line coach Chris Kuper, who replaced legendary coach Jeff Stoutland, has also failed to get Philly's front five back to the play that dominated two seasons ago. After seven straight losses, Eagles executive vice president Howie Roseman will have to decide which players best to trade and who to keep with the 2027 and beyond in mind. Here's who Roseman might look to move and how the 2027 NFL Draft current looks for the Eagles: When is the NFL trade deadline? This year, the NFL traded deadline is set for Tuesday, Nov. 10. All trades must be finalized by 4 p.m. ET of that day. Who could the Eagles trade at the NFL trade deadline? With an aging and underperforming roster, the Eagles could look to deal a number of veterans to help rebuild for the 2027 season. Here's a look at which players could be available: Saquon Barkley, RB While the former league-leading rusher has name value, it's unlikely Barkley, 29, is dealt since he's been banged up this season and has a promise from the team he won't be traded. Zack Baun, LB Another player who likely won't be traded but could fetch a decent return because of his high level of play. Baun, 29, has $11 million and $27 million cap hits in 2027 and 2028. Landon Dickerson, OL Much like former linemate Cam Jurgens, the Eagles could look to deal Dickerson, 28, if another team believes he has something left in the tank after injuries has hurt his play the last two-plus seasons. Dallas Goedert, TE After surprisingly returning the Eagles on a reduced salary in the offseason, the often-productive pass catcher could be an enticing piece to a contending team. Geodert, 31, is a free agent after the season. Moro Ojomo, DT Ojomo, an overachiever since being selected in the seventh round of the 2023 draft, would be an attractive team seeking another lineman who can provided pressure on defense. However, the Eagles have made it known that they prefer to try to extend Ojomo despite already doling out big contracts to defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Carter. item.title: Browns reveal Shedeur Sanders-Deshaun Watson decision for Week 10 less than 24 hours after loss
item.description: The Cleveland Browns appear ready to return to Deshaun Watson at quarterback for NFL Week 10, despite Shedeur Sanders delivering an impressive performance in Sunday’s overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints. The Browns plan to start Deshaun Watson in Week 10 vs the Texans, per source. Shedeur Sanders filled in Sunday in New Orleans, but returning to Watson was the expected move once he cleared concussion protocol. — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) November 9, 2026 The reported decision comes less than 24 hours after Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns, giving Cleveland’s coaching staff an interesting quarterback situation heading into its matchup against the Houston Texans. MORE: 3 NFL teams that should be worried after Week 9 Browns plan to return to Deshaun Watson against Texans Nov 1, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) looks to pass the ball during the first quarter of an NFL game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Browns plan to start Watson in Week 10 against Houston. Sanders filled in for Watson on Sunday after the veteran quarterback entered concussion protocol, but returning to Watson appears to be the move once he is medically cleared. Watson had started Cleveland’s first eight games before missing Sunday’s contest. The Browns had previously indicated that he would remain the starter once healthy, making this decision consistent with the team’s original plan. However, the timing is noteworthy considering how Sanders performed against New Orleans. The rookie quarterback completed 19 of 31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns without throwing an interception. He also helped Cleveland force overtime after trailing late in regulation. Sanders gave the Browns an opportunity to win, but the team ultimately fell 23-22 after failing to convert a two-point attempt in overtime. The offense found more success pushing the football downfield, particularly during the second half and overtime. Rookie wide receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston also benefited from Sanders’ willingness to attack downfield. Concepcion hauled in a 64-yard touchdown reception, while Boston made a 60-yard catch that helped spark Cleveland’s offensive production. item.title: Dianna Russini finally answers the question football fans are asking
item.description: Dianna Russini finally answers the question football fans are asking originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Seven months after having her career upended amid rumors of an alleged romantic relationship with Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, longtime NFL reporter Diana Russini is once more preparing for her close-up. Russini, who is married, largely stayed in the shadows as the fallout played out, opting against commenting publicly on the scandal throughout the offseason and start of the regular season. That was a marked departure from Vrabel's actions. The New England boss, who is also married, addressed reporters on multiple occasions, revealing in April that he was planning to go to counseling. Russini has been biding her time on the proverbial sidelines for the past few months. item.title: Mahomes And Kelce Set New NFL Record For QB-TE Yardage Duo
item.description: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs secured a historic milestone during their 35-12 victory over the New York Jets on Sunday, November 8. No other quarterback-tight end duo has exceeded the 9,360 receiving yards achieved by Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, according to reports. This achievement surpassed the previous mark held by Philip Rivers and Antonio Gates, It took 14 seasons to reach the same total. Mahomes and Kelce accomplished the feat in just eight and a half seasons, according to the CBS broadcast coverage of the game. While the record stood out, the physical toll on Mahomes during the contest drew immediate attention from the team. The quarterback played through an elbow injury that caused visible concern late in the first half. Before halftime ended, he returned to the field, completed a 12-yard pass to Kelce and then ran for seven yards. Center Creed Humphrey addressed the situation in the locker room after the game, noting the impact of the quarterback’s resilience on the rest of the offense. A Record Built on Speed It took Rivers and Gates 14 years to build their yardage total, whereas Tom Brady and Rob Gronkowski accomplished theirs in just 11 seasons. Mahomes and Kelce have outpaced both legendary duos in less than half the time. The pair reached the mark on a 38-yard connection between the two players during the second quarter. Elbow Concerns and Medical Updates Despite the historic offensive output, the health of the franchise quarterback remains the primary story for the upcoming week. Mahomes admitted that his throwing motion was not ideal during the first half of the game. He noted that the swelling and fluid in his elbow made it difficult to throw the ball the way he wanted initially. “I felt like out of half, I wasn’t throwing the ball the way I wanted to,” Mahomes said regarding his performance during the early stages of the contest. Medical tests were conducted after the game. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that an MRI performed on Mahomes did not show signs of a major injury. “Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes underwent an MRI following today’s win and sources say the tests did not reveal a major injury,” Rapoport wrote. The plan now shifts to managing the elbow strain and reducing swelling before the team travels to face the Atlanta Falcons. Defensive Stars Join the History Books While the offense set a new standard, the defense also made significant progress on Sunday. Defensive tackle Chris Jones recorded two sacks against the Jets, bringing his career total to 90.5. This performance moved him past Hall of Famer Tamba Hali for the second-most sacks in franchise history. Jones credited his teammates for the milestone, emphasizing that the record is a collective effort rather than an individual accomplishment. “It’s a testament to all my teammates,” Jones said after the game. The defense recorded five total sacks, the most the unit has achieved in a single game this season. The Chiefs play their next ga

item.title: NASA just launched a $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge to award cash prizes to students that solve lunar base problems
item.description: null CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there's $1 million in prizes up for grabs for the winners. To build and sustain a base on the moon , NASA will have to solve a myriad of problems. And they're looking to the next generation for help, the space agency's chief Jared Isaacman said Sunday (Nov. 8). "We are inviting students from across the country to help solve some of the problems that stand between humanity and a permanent presence on another world," Isaacman said. "We're putting 1 million in prizes together to support the best ideas and recognize the teams behind them." Isaacman made this announcement wearing his blue flight suit from the rocket garden at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center amidst the agency's MAX POWER air show event . Just the day before, he flew fighter jets in that suit and even jumped out of a plane, skydiving into the event. Soon after this announcement, he was flying another fighter plane above the crowd. The audience for this announcement was filled with students of all ages. Some young children wearing costume spacesuits squeezed as close as they could to the front of the room while teenagers considering their futures listened intently. It was clear that Isaacman's presence and words were landing with this group. But what moon base challenges does NASA want to see these students tackle? In short, all of them. "The moon base will allow us to conduct groundbreaking science, test new technologies, and prepare again for where we inevitably go next, which is the red planet," he said. "But before any of that can happen, we have an awful lot of problems that need to be solved." "We need ways to generate power through the long lunar night . We need to protect our astronauts from that incredibly harsh and dangerous and demanding environment on the surface. We need to move people and equipment around on the surface and support human life three days away from Earth," Isaacman said, illustrating just a few of the big issues that present with the concept of a moon base. NASA Adminisrator Jared Isaacman invites students to help NASA build a moon base at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center. (Image credit: Chelsea Gohd) How will it work? This challenge is open to high school and post-secondary students based in the U.S. For participating students, they will form teams that will work on an idea from one of six different technical topics related to creating and running a moon base. These six topics include power systems, habitats, communications, mobility, life support and astronaut safety . This will be what Isaacman described as a "multi-phase competition that mirrors how ideas are developed actually in the aerospace industry." "Teams will first submit concepts, then they're going to refine them, and finalists will have the opportunity to present their solutions directly to NASA leaders and stakeholders,"

item.title: Machine learning researchers build a better world model
item.description: Machine learning researchers have developed a technique that allows world models to make better predictions about how objects will behave. World models are used to train physical AI systems like robots how to navigate the real world. They predict the consequences of actions. But they do so based on observed data. These models could provide better direction to robots if they were able to make inferences about possible actions without being trained for all the possible outcomes. Randall Balestriero (Brown University, AMI Labs), Kerda Varaku, and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun (NYU, AMI Labs) describe an approach that might allow that to happen in a pre-print paper, "Counterfactual World Models: Natura Non Facit Saltus." The Latin refers to Gottfried Leibniz's axiom " nature makes no leaps ," which had a good run until it ran headlong into quantum mechanics. Yet for the authors, the saying explains how they have been able to devise a method for zero-shot physics inference. Counterfactual world models, said Balestriero in an email to The Register use "the mismatch between your prediction and the real world to figure out what did you get wrong, and from that you can better understand what happened for better future predictions, debugging, reasoning, all at test time." Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture ( JEPA ) models, developed by LeCunn and colleagues back in 2023, have been proposed for robots because they can take an action as input and ask what the world would be like with that action. But a JEPA world model produces an average of outcomes and would not be able to anticipate counterfactual scenarios – events that didn't happen. The technique that the researchers developed is not specific to JEPAs – it can be applied to any world model that predicts the average next state under any action. But JEPA models are particularly well suited to being adapted. Balestriero said that the counterfactual world model experiments were done using off-the-shelf encoders (DINOv2 and MAE) without any fine-tuning and only a small predictor trained on top. Creating a counterfactual world model from that starting point would only require minor additions. Counterfactual world models predict alternative scenarios more effectively by inferring possibilities from what did occur. "In causal inference, answering 'What would have happened had I acted differently?' takes three steps," explained Balestriero. "You use what you observed to learn something about those hidden factors, you change the action, and you predict again with the hidden factors kept exactly as they were. "Our counterfactual world model does all three steps with one subtraction." Balestriero cited an example from the paper: a boat crossing a river with a hidden current and how the JEPA world model and counterfactual world model predicted the boat's movements. "The world model predicted where the boat would end up after steering left, and it actually ended up two meters further downstream," he explained.

item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — The Managing Director/Chief Executive of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), Mr Oluwaseun Faleye, has said that Nigeria cannot develop sustainable, globally competitive enterprises without safeguarding the workers who drive them. ‎ ‎Faleye said this on Monday in his goodwill message at the Grow Nigerian Conference 2026, held at the Ecobank Pan African Centre (EPAC), Victoria Island, Lagos, under the theme “The Next Frontier for Innovation, Policy and Market Access.” ‎ ‎The three-day conference, convened by the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria, SMEDAN under the leadership of Director-General/CEO Mr. Charles Odii, brought representatives of the Federal Government, development partners, business leaders, and entrepreneurs. ‎ ‎While commending SMEDAN for sustaining the platform, Faleye said the theme was timely, as it challenges Nigeria to move beyond business creation to building enterprises that are productive, resilient and capable of generating sustainable employment. ‎ ‎Painting a vivid picture of the Nigerian entrepreneur, Faleye highlighted the manufacturer in Aba struggling to scale, the woman processor in Kano searching for new markets, and the young tech founder in Lagos with global ambitions. He described MSMEs as employers, innovators, and the economic lifeline of families and communities, stressing that they must remain at the heart of Nigeria’s economic transformation agenda. ‎ ‎He, however, acknowledged the harsh operating environment in Nigeria, citing high energy costs, inflation, exchange rate pressures, limited access to affordable financing, inadequate infrastructure and logistics challenges as some of them. ‎According to him: “The challenge is not simply to encourage people to start businesses, but to create an environment in which those businesses can survive, expand, compete and prosper.” ‎ ‎He argued that enterprise development discourse must also answer a critical question: what happens to the people who make those businesses grow? ‎ ‎He said: “Behind every successful enterprise are people whose skills, commitment and labour sustain its operations. A business cannot truly be considered sustainable if its economic success is achieved at the expense of the safety, dignity and wellbeing of its workforce”. ‎ ‎He explained that the NSITF administers the Employees’ Compensation Scheme under the Employees’ Compensation Act, 2010, which provides compensation, medical support, rehabilitation and income replacement to workers who suffer work-related injuries, diseases, disability or death. ‎ ‎Faleye clarified that the scheme is funded by employers’ contribution of one per cent of total monthly payroll, and is not deducted from employees’ salaries. ‎ ‎“Protecting workers is also good for business. item.title: Netflix announces 'Stranger Things' spin-off 'Other Worlds', and it's already teasing a trip to Area 51 (video)
item.description: null So, you thought "Stranger Things" was done and dusted after all that Conformity Gate nonsense? No way! Netflix's sci-fi sensation returns in the live-action prequel series "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure." Created by the Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry, with the episodes set to be directed by Joe Wright ("Darkest Hour", "Black Mirror"), this new show isn't set in Hawkins or the electric '80s. No, this time around, the action takes place in Marion, Nevada, in 1955, and you know what else is located in Nevada, right? Area 51 . The teaser trailer certainly teases the possibility of a trip to the world's most paradoxically famous secret military base, showcasing a bike and radio resting outside of a fence with a sign that clearly says it's a restricted area (in any TV show or film, that's actually an invitation to see what's on the other side). Of course, the tease doesn't end there, as the thunder booms in the sky and there's a visual hint of a wormhole. No story details about "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" have been released to date, but there are some clues out there for all the Internet sleuths. Trefrey wrote the Henry Creel-focused "Stranger Things: The First Shadow" play, while Matt Duffer explained to Variety how a spin-off show would tackle the rock that Henry found in the briefcase in "Stranger Things." So, yes, expect this to be a Henry-centric affair and the start of his long, hard road to hell and becoming Vecna. (Image credit: Netflix) What'll be interesting, though, is to see how the show ties into the history of Area 51. After all, it was on April 12, 1955, that CIA officer Richard Bissell discovered the site, while the "Other Worlds" trailer has the date of April 19th clearly marked onscreen, so the timelines align nicely here. "Stranger Things" has never been shy of tying itself to real-world science and historical events, so it'll be fascinating to see how the show explores Area 51 as a concept and the secrets everybody believes are hidden there. Was it really a site to test highly advanced weapons and aircraft, or was E.T. 's cousin held hostage there until he revealed Colonel Sanders' 11 herbs and spices? Who knows, with all this renewed excitement around this mysterious military facility, we might get another "Storm Area 51" event to enjoy and laugh at all over again. Regardless, more "Stranger Things" is welcome news, and since it's presumably about one of the show's best characters, Henry Creel, it only adds another layer to his already intriguing lore. If we can't have an origin story about Hopper's incredible and envious moustache, this is the next best thing. "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" arrives on Netflix in 2028. item.title: ‘Student is alive’ – Babcock University clarifies viral hall incident
item.description: Babcock University has confirmed that a student involved in an incident at one of its halls of residence is alive and responding to treatment, dismissing reports that he had died. The university, in an official statement signed by Johnson B. Akintayo, AVP, Communication, Media and Branding, said the student was receiving medical attention at the Babcock University Teaching Hospital. Official Statement: Update on the Hall Incident Babcock University confirms that the student involved is alive, responding well to treatment, and receiving the necessary medical care. His parents are on campus with him. Please read the full statement attached. pic.twitter.com/xsMQhWcA2z — Babcock University, Ilishan-Remo, Nigeria (@Babcock_Univ) November 9, 2026 “Contrary to reports suggesting that the student may have died, we wish to assure the public that he is responding positively to treatment and is receiving the necessary medical care,” the statement said. The incident occurred at one of the university’s student residential facilities. According to the institution, the situation was brought under control through the prompt intervention of the student’s roommates, whose actions prevented a potentially worse outcome. The university also disclosed that one of the students who participated in the rescue sustained injuries and was immediately taken for medical attention. It said the injured student’s parents had been contacted and were on campus to support their son as he received treatment. “The other student who sustained injury while rescuing his roommate, has been treated and discharged,” the statement added. Babcock University said it had commenced an investigation to establish the immediate and underlying circumstances surrounding the incident. The investigation, it explained, would help determine what happened, identify possible contributing factors and establish measures to prevent a recurrence. The institution also urged members of the public and media organisations to avoid spreading unverified information or attributing causes to the incident while investigations were ongoing. Beyond medical treatment, the university said it was committed to supporting the student’s recovery and well-being. “Babcock University takes the safety, health and welfare of its students and employees seriously,” the statement said. The institution further commended the student’s roommates for their courage and swift intervention, while appealing for sensitivity and restraint in discussions about the incident. It added that it would continue to monitor the student’s recovery and take necessary steps to establish the facts surrounding the incident. item.title: Social unrest ahead of French elections: Protesters 'don't believe politics can achieve anything'
item.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University. France's 1.6% minimum-wage increase, in response to the countrywide protests, may offer a temporary reprieve from social unrest, but it does little to resolve the deeper political and institutional crisis confronting the country. According to Foucart, the central problem extends beyond declining purchasing power, fiscal constraints and the limitations of a minority government. It concerns a growing loss of faith in politics itself. “They are in the street because they don't believe politics can achieve anything,” Foucart argues, suggesting that the persistence of mass demonstrations ahead of the presidential election reflects profound disillusionment with the political system's capacity to deliver meaningful change.

item.title: Microsoft takes three decades to make Sticky Keys less sticky
item.description: Windows testers are getting a new option in the Sticky Keys and Filter Keys dialogs – one to banish the pop-ups without needing to venture deep into Settings. It's only taken several decades for Microsoft to put the off switch where the interruption actually happens. The accessibility features themselves are useful, though triggering their activation prompts by accident is another matter. Once enabled, Sticky Keys let users press modifier keys (such as Control) one at a time instead of holding them down together. For example, rather than holding Control and pressing C to copy, a user can press and release Control, then press C. Filter Keys, meanwhile, ignores brief or repeated keystrokes and adjusts the keyboard's repeat behavior. However, the dialogs are of little use to people who don't need the features, and they can pop up at the most inconvenient moments. Tap Shift five times, and you'll see what we mean: Windows chimes and shows a dialog asking whether you'd like to turn on Sticky Keys. Dismiss it, hit Shift five times, and there it is again. Or hold down the right Shift key for eight seconds to be treated to the Filter Keys pop-up. You can stop this behavior elsewhere in the system, but it requires a trek through Windows settings. The change, introduced in the Experimental Windows Insider Build 26340.9882, adds an option to the Sticky Keys or Filter Keys dialogs to dismiss the prompts permanently. It's a small change, but one that should spare users an irritating interruption. Better late than never – even if "never ask me again" has taken roughly three decades to reach the dialog. Former Microsoft engineer Charles Opperman said he wrote the dialog in early 1995 "after @bradsilverberg kids kept activating StickeyKeys [sic] while playing Space Cadet pinball." Opperman added that a link to Settings was added in Windows 98 or what would become Windows 2000, and a checkbox was considered even then, but it wasn't deemed a priority. Users could turn off the prompt via settings. Now the option is front and center. The option is also rolling out in the Windows Insider Beta channel , although Microsoft has not announced a general release date. ®

item.title: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Rivers and Delta actually show
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Rivers and Delta states, neighbours in the South-South, backed different presidential candidates in the February 25, 2023 election, according to results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal * What is 25% requirement in Nigeria’s presidential election? Bola Ahmed Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, won Rivers, while Peter Obi, who ran on the Labour Party, LP, ticket, won Delta. Rivers: Tinubu ahead by 56,520 votes Tinubu polled 231,591 votes in Rivers, ahead of Obi’s 175,071. That put the APC candidate 56,520 votes clear of the runner-up. Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, came third with 88,468 votes. Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, trailed with 1,322. Delta: Obi’s commanding lead Delta produced the wider margin. Obi scored 341,866 votes, against 161,600 for Atiku, a lead of 180,266 votes. Tinubu managed 90,183 votes in Delta and finished third. Kwankwaso had 3,122. What the two results show together Taken together, the states reverse each other’s order. Tinubu won Rivers but placed third in Delta, while Obi won Delta and was runner-up in Rivers. Obi was the only candidate to finish in the top two in both states. The combined figures tell a different story from the two state winners alone. Obi polled 516,937 votes across Rivers and Delta, compared with Tinubu’s 321,774. This is a difference of 195,163 votes in Obi’s favour, even though Tinubu took the state with the higher turnout of the two. Obi’s vote in Delta alone, at 341,866, exceeded Tinubu’s combined total for both states by 20,092 votes. Atiku polled 250,068 votes across the two states, finishing third in Rivers and second in Delta. Kwankwaso placed fourth in both, with 4,444 votes combined. Tinubu’s support was uneven. He polled 231,591 votes in Rivers but only 90,183 in Delta, a drop of 141,408 votes between the two neighbouring states. Vanguard News The post Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Rivers and Delta actually show appeared first on Vanguard News .
