item.title: COP31: WMO warns El Niño could push 2027 temperatures higher
item.description: The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) has warned that 2027 could become the hottest year on record as an unusually strong El Niño combines with the effects of climate change to push global temperatures higher. WMO Secretary-General, Celeste Saulo, gave the warning on Monday while presenting the organisation’s State of the Climate Update 2026 at a news conference during the ongoing COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye. Saulo said the past 12 years had been the warmest on record, with the last four years, including 2026, ranking as the hottest. She disclosed that global average temperatures between January and September 2026 were approximately 1.47 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. According to her, the developing 2026/2027 El Niño is unusually strong, with sea-surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific expected to approach four times the 0.5-degree threshold used to declare the climate phenomenon. “Indeed, this 2026/2027 El Niño is off the charts. It is different from any El Niño that we have monitored,” she said. The WMO chief explained that El Niño typically has its greatest impact on global temperatures in the following year, raising concerns that 2027 could surpass previous temperature records. She also revealed that ocean heat content had reached a record high for the 10th consecutive year, while global sea levels had risen to unprecedented levels, exposing about 900 million people living in low-lying coastal areas to increasing risks. Saulo warned that extreme heat, tropical cyclones and intense rainstorms were becoming more severe, exposing millions of people to dangerous weather conditions in 2026. She cited heatwaves across India, Pakistan, other parts of Asia and North America, as well as tens of thousands of excess deaths recorded in Europe. “The human and economic cost is unacceptably high,” she said. Saulo called on governments participating in COP31 to strengthen global climate observation systems and increase funding for early-warning mechanisms. She noted that the number of countries reporting multi-hazard early-warning systems had increased from 56 in 2015 to 136 in 2025. “We cannot afford to fly blind,” she said, emphasising the need for sustained climate monitoring to anticipate extreme weather events and protect vulnerable populations. Also speaking, the UN Climate Change Executive Secretary, Simon Stiell, described the climate crisis as a global health emergency, warning that extreme heat, pollution and climate-related disasters were placing increasing pressure on healthcare systems. Stiell said heatwaves during the northern hemisphere’s summer had killed an estimated 50,000 people across Europe, while hundreds of millions of people in southern Asia were exposed to extreme heat. “The climate crisis is now a global health crisis of pandemic proportions,” he said. He highlighted the dangers of extreme heat to pregnant women, newborns and maternal health, linking the growing risks to continued fossil fu

item.title: Full list: Messi makes FIFPRO World 11 as Ronaldo misses out
item.description: Lionel Messi has been named in the 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World 11, extending his record as the most-selected player in the award’s history, while Cristiano Ronaldo failed to make the final team. Messi returns to the prestigious team for the first time since 2023, taking his record number of appearances to 18. The Argentine first made the selection in 2007 and has continued to earn recognition from fellow professional footballers across successive generations. Barcelona youngster Lamine Yamal also made history after becoming the first player to earn two FIFPRO World 11 selections before turning 20. The Spain international was also included in last year’s team. Yamal joins fellow Spanish players David Raya, Pau Cubarsi and Rodri in the 2026 selection, taking Spain’s record tally of Men’s World 11 appearances to 53. The team was unveiled following votes from 19,806 professional male footballers across 73 countries, making it one of the few major football awards decided exclusively by players. Since 2005, FIFPRO has invited professional footballers worldwide to vote for the players they believe have delivered the most impressive performances during the assessment period. 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World 11 Goalkeeper David Raya (Arsenal, Spain) Defenders Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona, Spain) Achraf Hakimi (Paris Saint-Germain, Morocco) Nuno Mendes (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Midfielders Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid, England) Rodri (Manchester City/Barcelona, Spain) Vitinha (Paris Saint-Germain, Portugal) Forwards Erling Haaland (Manchester City, Norway) Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid, France) Lionel Messi (Inter Miami, Argentina) Lamine Yamal (Barcelona, Spain) How the voting worked Professional footballers cast their votes through a secure digital platform provided by FIFPRO and its affiliated player unions. For the 2026 edition, players were assessed based on their performances between August 4, 2025, and July 19, 2026. To qualify, footballers must have featured in at least 30 official matches during the period. Each voter selected their three best performers in four categories: goalkeeper, defender, midfielder and forward. The goalkeeper and the three players with the most votes in each of the defensive, midfield and attacking categories secured their places in the team. The final position was awarded to the remaining outfield player with the highest number of votes. item.title: BlackRock: Security Fears Are Driving Bitcoin Whales Into IBIT
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine BlackRock: Security Fears Are Driving Bitcoin Whales Into IBIT Large bitcoin holders are swapping coins they guard themselves for shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) at a record pace, the firm’s head of digital assets said Monday, as kidnappings and hacks push security to the top of their list. “The current moment is the highest we’ve seen at any point,” Robbie Mitchnick told Barron’s , adding that demand for the swaps “has sort of been one way — up.” Of all the reasons clients give, he said, “the single largest one is security and peace of mind.” The trades are in-kind conversions. A holder delivers bitcoin to the fund through an intermediary and receives newly created IBIT shares, without first selling the coins for cash. BlackRock relies on Galaxy Digital, Talos and Virtu to handle the transactions, and those firms set the minimum size. Barron’s put the volume BlackRock has seen at $3.6 billion, noting the real figure could be larger because the firm does not process every conversion itself. Mitchnick cited a bigger number in August, telling Bloomberg that IBIT had facilitated more than $5 billion of such swaps, up from more than $3 billion in October 2025 . In that August interview, BlackRock’s Mitchnick named the threats outright: “People see things happen in the outside world — whether it’s kidnappings, ransom, custody failures — that motivate them to make this switch for all or some of their holdings.” He told Barron’s the recent Binance hack was not news to big holders. “Most large Bitcoin holders were already acutely aware of the risk of holding on an exchange and in a hot wallet,” he said. How BlackRock’s swaps became possible The SEC voted on July 29, 2025, to let spot bitcoin and ether funds create and redeem shares in kind, ending the cash-only structure it required when the funds launched in January 2024. Access has widened since. BlackRock’s minimum started around $30 million and now hovers between $1 million and $2 million, Barron’s reported. Taxes are part of the pitch. Converting appreciated bitcoin into IBIT in kind “generally isn’t seen as a sale that would trigger capital-gains taxes,” Barron’s wrote, while Bloomberg cautioned that avoiding an immediate bill depends on the investor’s circumstances. Mitchnick also pointed to estate planning, calling it “much, much simpler” to hold the exposure “within the confines of their private bank.” Once inside, the coins sit with IBIT’s custodian, an affiliate of Coinbase Prime, in what Mitchnick called an “institutional-grade cold-storage model.” The fund held 795,921 BTC, worth about $60.4 billion, as of Nov. 6. Why the flow numbers overstate demand An in-kind creation adds IBIT shares and counts toward the fund’s reported flows, but no bitcoin is bought on the open market. The coins already existed and simply changed wrappers, so headline flow figures overstate new cash. Cash has been moving the other way. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.28 billion

item.title: Ethiopian Airlines, Air Peace sign interline agreement to boost connectivity
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Africa’s leading aviation group, Ethiopian Airlines, and Nigeria’s leading carrier, Air Peace, have signed a bilateral interline agreement, strengthening air transport connectivity across Africa and expanding travel opportunities for passengers. The partnership enables each airline to issue tickets for eligible itineraries that include flights operated by both carriers, providing customers with a more convenient and integrated travel experience. Through this collaboration, passengers will be able to book qualifying journeys on a single ticket and enjoy through-checked baggage to their destination, where applicable. Commenting on the partnership, Ethiopian Airlines Group Mr Mesfin Tasew, said “We are delighted to partner with Air Peace, a leading carrier in Nigeria, through this strategic interline agreement. This collaboration reflects our shared commitment to enhancing connectivity, improving customer convenience, and supporting the growth of air travel across the African continent. By combining our strengths, we are creating more travel opportunities and bringing Africa closer to the world.” For his part, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Air Peace, Allen Onyema, said: “This partnership with Ethiopian Airlines represents another significant milestone in our commitment to strengthening Africa’s aviation connectivity and bringing the continent closer together. By combining Air Peace’s extensive domestic, regional network, and our growing international network with Ethiopian Airlines’ global reach, we are creating greater opportunities for seamless travel in and out of the African continent. Beyond expanding travel options, this collaboration reflects our shared vision of fostering stronger economic, commercial and cultural ties across Africa and beyond. At Air Peace, we remain committed to building strategic partnerships that enhance passenger convenience, broaden connectivity and position African aviation as a formidable force in global air transport.” Meanwhile, the streamlined process eliminates the need for separate bookings and baggage re-checks, creating a smoother and more efficient travel experience. The agreement links Air Peace’s domestic and regional network with Ethiopian Airlines’ vast international network spanning Africa, Europe, Asia, the Middle East and the Americas. As a result, travellers departing from major Nigerian and west African cities will gain seamless access to Ethiopian Airlines’ global destinations through Addis Ababa, while international passengers arriving on Ethiopian Airlines flights will benefit from expanded onward travel options across Nigeria and west africa through Air Peace’s domestic network. item.title: Wike criticises ADC over reaction to court judgment
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, on Monday criticised the African Democratic Congress (ADC) over its comments on the court judgment that removed the Senator David Mark-led executive committee of the party. Wike spoke at a town hall interactive meeting with political stakeholders, traditional rulers and residents of Kwali Area Council of the FCT. He said political parties should serve as vehicles for development and good governance rather than platforms for persistent internal conflicts. The minister also accused opposition politicians of placing personal ambitions above the welfare and development of the people. “Isn’t it that a party is a vehicle that you enter intentionally to go where you are going? When you get there, you talk about development, you talk about good governance, and how you can bring welfare to your people,” he said. Wike commended area council chairmen and political leaders across party lines who had agreed to work together in the interest of the FCT. He urged residents to reject politicians who only appear during election periods with promises, calling on them to support leaders whose performance could be assessed through infrastructure delivery and empowerment initiatives. The minister said the administration of President Bola Tinubu had taken steps to address the country’s economic challenges and grant the FCT greater administrative autonomy. He cited the establishment of the FCT Civil Service Commission, appointment of an indigene of the territory as Head of Service and removal of the FCT from the Treasury Single Account (TSA) as examples of the administration’s achievements. Wike assured residents that the administration would take difficult decisions where necessary to deliver critical infrastructure, complete abandoned road projects and expand political representation for the people of the FCT. The meeting was attended by the Executive Chairman of Kwali Area Council, Nuhu Daniel Kwali; traditional rulers led by the Etsu of Kwali, Luka Ayedoo Nizassan III; councillors and representatives of the six area councils of the FCT. item.title: 2027: APC govt has built Nigeria for the benefit of few – Makinde
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Seyi Makinde, has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of building a country that works only for those in power, challenging the ruling government to explain what it has achieved for Nigerians in three years. Makinde said the administration had failed to deliver a country that worked for ordinary Nigerians, alleging that its newly promoted reform agenda merely repackaged ideas already advanced by the APM. He urged voters to reject what he described as a government serving the interests of a privileged few. Speaking on Monday at the party’s presidential campaign rally in Jos, Plateau State, the former Oyo State governor accused the ruling government of appropriating his party’s ideas. “When we unveiled our RESET Agenda, I said in Abuja that they would soon start stealing our ideas. Now they have started. They say theirs is ‘Reform to Prosperity’. They now say they want a Nigeria that will work for everybody. What have they been doing over the past three years? “They have built a Nigeria that works only for them. Send the oppressors packing. Send them back to Lagos, and let us bring in the team that will reset Nigeria,” he said. Makinde identified insecurity as a major obstacle to Plateau’s economic potential, promising that an APM government would prioritise security, tourism and job creation. Reflecting on his experience of Jos’s pleasant evening weather, he said the state could become a major tourism destination if its security challenges were addressed. “Security is a major pillar of the RESET Agenda. Once we start attracting tourists, our economy on the Plateau will expand, and we will create jobs for our teeming youths,” he said. Urging supporters to take the party’s message to the grassroots, Makinde stressed that electoral victories were determined at polling-unit level. “Go back to your various units and spread the RESET message. Elections are won at the unit level. Go back to your units with the RESET message. If Nigeria is not working for you, then let us reset it. When we reset Nigeria, we will have a country that works for everybody,” he said. Earlier, the party’s vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, appealed to Plateau residents to support the APM, lamenting that insecurity had eroded the state’s reputation as a peaceful tourism destination. Recalling his frequent visits to the state in the past, Daura said the party was determined to restore its lost appeal. “Plateau has been a state of peace and tranquillity, a home of tourism where anything good used to be found. Personally, years back, I used to visit the Plateau at least three times a year. Unfortunately, some people have tried to spoil the Plateau. But we are here with our resolute agenda to set things right for the Plateau and for Nigeria,” he said. item.title: Toluwanisings laid to rest in Ibadan
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has been laid to rest at his residence in Ibadan, Oyo State, bringing an end to weeks of disagreement among members of his family over his final resting place. The gospel artiste was buried on Monday, November 9, 2026, in a private ceremony attended by family members following a funeral service at Banjola Event and Conference Centre, Alakia, Ibadan. His burial came after a disagreement between his widow, Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola, and his paternal relatives over where his remains should be interred. While his paternal family had expressed concerns about the circumstances surrounding his death and initially pushed for his burial in Ikirun, Osun State, his widow and associates were involved in discussions over the final arrangements. The disagreement attracted public attention and eventually prompted the intervention of the Oyo State Police Command. On November 3, the parties involved signed a peace undertaking at the police command headquarters in Eleyele, Ibadan, agreeing to avoid further public exchanges and actions capable of escalating tensions. Speaking on the agreement, the police command stated that, “All parties agreed to maintain peace and be of good behaviour, refrain from any act capable of causing a breach of the peace.” The intervention paved the way for the family to settle on burying the singer at his Ibadan residence, where his wife and children live. Toluwanisings, who was widely recognised for his energetic worship ministrations and gospel songs, including A Very Big God, died on October 14, 2026. His death generated reactions across the gospel music community, while the disagreement surrounding his burial further drew public attention to the family’s situation. item.title: MAX POWER: NASA’s Inaugural Aerospace Expo Ignites America’s Future
item.description: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman skydives into the agency’s MAX POWER expo and air show on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The agency’s inaugural MAX POWER is an aerospace festival celebrating the past, present, and future of flight and space exploration in honor of America’s 250th anniversary. Credit: NASA/Jonathan Shaban Thousands gathered over several days in early November to experience MAX POWER – NASA’s first exhibition of America’s superiority in space, aeronautics, and technology on and around the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The multi-day, family-friendly event honored the nation’s 250th anniversary and served as a culmination of the agency’s Inspiration Tour . Among the many highlights, NASA welcomed President Donald J. Trump to MAX POWER, which featured flyovers and a skydive from NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, and announced a new X-plane, astronaut candidate recruitment, a student Moon Base challenge, and discussed the agency’s latest lunar exploration plans. “It was a great week at NASA Kennedy, where we were joined by the President and federal, state, international, and industry leaders,” said Isaacman. “During our nation’s 250th birthday, the year of Artemis II’s voyage around the Moon, we were thrilled to invite the public out to see the rockets, the landers, the rovers, and the technology that will return astronauts to the lunar surface and build the base, not to mention witness a wonderful airshow that included NASA research aircraft and was headlined by the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds.” Through multiple park experiences, NASA and external collaborators at UP.Summit, Air Dot Show, Purpose Entertainment, and Delaware North each hosted a variety of private and public events Nov. 4-8. Teams showcased the newest aircraft, rovers, autonomous vehicles, and technologies defining the future of air and space. Astronauts, scientists, engineers, pilots, and subject matter experts were on hand for a variety of moderated discussions, appearances, and more. Some of the key announcements made at MAX POWER included: NASA opened astronaut applications through Thursday, Dec. 3, seeking future explorers to fly Artemis and low Earth orbit missions, and help build humanity’s first lunar outpost. NASA also challenged students to a $1 million competition to design innovative solutions for the Moon Base, giving participants an opportunity to develop necessary skills for careers in the space industry while helping advance new concepts for Moon Base technologies. Agency leadership announced numerous awards, task orders, and selections involving 12 companies to advance development of the Moon Base , marking significant progress toward establishing humanity’s first permanent presence on the lunar surface. The announcements spanned transportation, technology, and science initiatives, including moving forward with development of PROMISE, NASA’s nuclear-powered lunar rover. item.title: 2027 will test clarity of Nigeria’s legal framework on electoral justice – INEC
item.description: …warns AI, digital threats may spill into courtrooms … as 375 tribunal judges take oath By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on Monday said the 2027 general elections would test not only its operational preparedness but also the effectiveness and clarity of the nation’s legal framework for electoral justice. According to the Commission, the political stability of the nation will depend not only on how efficiently it conducts elections, but equally on how courageously, transparently and justly the judiciary adjudicates the disputes that follow. The Chairman of the electoral body, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, spoke at the opening ceremony of a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the 2027 election petition tribunals held at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja. The workshop was preceded by the inauguration of 375 judges who will serve on tribunals that will hear election petitions filed by aggrieved parties across the country. Section 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, vests in the President of the Court of Appeal the responsibility of constituting Election Petition Tribunals for the adjudication of disputes arising from National and State Houses of Assembly and Governorship elections. Similarly, Section 134(3)(a) and (b) of the Electoral Act, 2026, prescribes the timelines for constituting the tribunals and opening their registries. Describing the workshop’s theme, “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability,” as apt, the INEC Chairman stressed that, with the general election scheduled to commence on January 16, 2027, the Commission recognises that the legitimacy of the country’s constitutional democracy rests upon impartial electoral administration and fearless judicial adjudication. He said: “While INEC manages the ballot, deploys technology, and safeguards the voter franchise, the Election Petition Tribunals stand as the ultimate guardians of democratic legitimacy. “When political contestations overflow from polling units into the courtroom, the Judiciary provides the constitutional sanctuary where grievances are transformed into peace, unlawful shortcuts are corrected, and the sovereign choice of the electorate is vindicated under the Rule of Law. “The credibility of elections cannot be measured solely by the conduct of voting or the declaration of results. It depends equally on public confidence that electoral disputes will be determined independently, fairly and in accordance with the law. “Citizens must be assured not only that their votes count, but also that the legal system is capable of protecting their democratic choices. “The consequences of electoral judgments frequently extend beyond candidates and political parties. They affect public confidence, the legitimacy of elected institutions and democratic stability. “Judicial scrutiny also provides an important mechanism of accountability for election administration. item.title: NASA’s ESCAPADE Completes Powered Earth Flybys, Now En Route to Mars
item.description: NASA’s two ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) spacecraft have each successfully completed a powered Earth flyby, using Earth’s gravity in combination with a sustained engine burn to slingshot themselves toward Mars. With these successful maneuvers complete, the twin spacecraft are on target to reach the Red Planet in September 2027. “This is the first time NASA has used a powered Earth flyby to propel a spacecraft toward Mars, and we’ve now executed this maneuver twice, flawlessly, in just two days,” said Asal Naseri, acting associate flight director for the Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video In November 2026, each of NASA’s two ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) spacecraft executed a powered flyby of Earth, combining Earth’s gravity with an engine burn, to slingshot itself toward Mars. The first spacecraft made its closest approach around 5 a.m. EST on Saturday, Nov. 7, and the second did so two days later, around 6 a.m. EST on Monday, Nov. 9. In this animation, each spacecraft’s approximately 9-minute trans-Mars injection burn appears as an orange arc along the spacecraft’s trajectory. Advanced Space/Matt Bolliger The two ESCAPADE spacecraft launched from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Nov. 13, 2025, when Earth and Mars were on opposite sides of the Sun. So instead of heading straight for the Red Planet, as most other Mars missions have done, both spacecraft entered a “loiter” or “Earth-proximity” orbit. They charted a first-of-its-kind, kidney-bean-shaped course around a place in space about a million miles from Earth called Lagrange point 2, which is a gravitational balancing point on the opposite side of Earth from the Sun. Then they headed back toward Earth to perform this gravitational slingshot maneuver around our planet once Earth and Mars were favorably aligned. To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The ESCAPADE mission is pioneering a unique path to get to Mars. After launch in November 2025, the two ESCAPADE spacecraft looped around the Earth-Sun Lagrange point 2 (L2), in an “Earth-proximity” or “loiter” orbit that allowed the spacecraft to return to Earth in November 2026 and use our planet’s gravity to slingshot themselves to Mars. Advanced Space/Matt Bolliger “With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, ESCAPADE is pioneering a new strategy for getting to Mars,” said Jeff Parker of Advanced Space, lead mission designer. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.” The first ESCAPADE spacecraft completed its close approach to Earth and its approximately 9-minute trans-Mars injection burn — the eng

Tariq is the Editor-in-Chief of Space.com based out of our New York City office and joined the team in 2001, first as an intern and staff writer, and later as an editor. He covers human spaceflight, exploration and space science, as well as skywatching and entertainment. He became Space.com's Managing Editor in 2009 and Editor-in-Chief in 2019. In October 2022, Tariq received the Harry Kolcum Award for excellence in space reporting from the National Space Club Florida Committee. In June 2025, the National Space Society awarded him the Space Pioneer Award for Excellence in Mass Media at the International Space Development Conference in Orlando, Florida.

Hailing from Stockton, California (where he attended the same high school as NASA astronaut Jose Hernandez), Tariq studied print journalism and astronomy at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, earning a bachelor's degree in journalism in 1999 along with a minor in astronomy. He then served as a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering education and city beats in La Habra and Fullerton in Orange County for the Our Times sections.

In 2000, Tariq became the city reporter for the Huntington Beach Independent, a weekly publication of the Los Angeles Times, covering local politics and events, crime, business and environmental issues. He left the Los Angeles Times in 2001 to study science journalism at New York University, where he earned a master's degree in 2002 from NYU's Science and Environmental Reporting Program (now the Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program) under the direction of space reporter William Burrows.

Tariq first joined Space.com as an intern in September 2001 while also serving as a research assistant for nutrition writer Gary Taubes and writing freelance projects, where his work appeared in The Scientist and Laboratory Equipment Magazine. He became a full-time reporter covering spaceflight in 2004, with this first launch being NASA's STS-114 Return to Flight mission in July 2005.

Tariq is also an Eagle Scout (yes, he has the Space Exploration merit badge) and went to Space Camp four times as a kid and a fifth time as an adult. When not writing about space, you can find Tariq watching the latest Star Trek TV series, sci-fi movies and reading about hippos, his favorite animal. You can find Tariq at Space.com and as the co-host to the This Week In Space podcast with space historian Rod Pyle on the TWiT network. To see his latest project, you can follow Tariq on Twitter @tariqjmalik.

item.title: Pat Utomi blasts Tinubu’s govt, asks what Nigerians pay taxes for
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Political economist Pat Utomi has accused the APC-led government of abandoning its responsibilities while Nigerians pay out of pocket for basic services, from electricity and water to roads, healthcare and education. In a post on his X handle on Monday, Utomi questioned what citizens receive in return for paying taxes when households and communities must fund services that government is expected to provide. “The only thing this APC-led government is good at doing is making your life worse,” he wrote. Utomi said Nigerians buy generators to cope with unreliable electricity, sink boreholes for water and contribute money to repair roads. He also cited private security, healthcare and schools as costs families increasingly bear because public institutions have been neglected. He added that waste disposal, drainage, streetlights and transformers had also become private financial responsibilities. “Then what exactly are we paying this APC-led government to do?” he asked, arguing that governments elsewhere invest public resources in education, healthcare, infrastructure and social welfare. Utomi also criticised the government’s appeals for patience and sacrifice amid economic hardship. He cited the removal of petrol subsidies and increases in electricity tariffs and university fees, alongside rising healthcare costs. “But how much more must the people sacrifice while those in power continue to enjoy the privileges of office?” he asked. Utomi argued that taxation obliges government to provide public services, describing it as more than a contribution from citizens to politicians. “The government cannot collect from the people, abandon its responsibilities and then demand applause from the people they’re making their lives difficult,” he wrote. He concluded with a challenge to the government: “If Nigerians must finance their own survival, what exactly is the purpose of government?” In a separate post on Sunday, Utomi said the APC government had made the daily struggle to earn a living an unbearable burden for hardworking Nigerians. He described the hardship as a tragedy for a richly endowed nation that he believes is poorly governed. He said: “The incompetence of the APC government has turned the daily struggle for survival into an unbearable burden for hardworking Nigerians. Those who labour honestly to earn a living are being punished by a system that should be making their lives easier. What a tragedy for a nation so richly endowed yet so poorly governed!” The post Pat Utomi blasts Tinubu’s govt, asks what Nigerians pay taxes for appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Binance to Close Accounts in Four EU Countries Dec. 31, Charging Idle Balances From Nov. 29
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance to Close Accounts in Four EU Countries Dec. 31, Charging Idle Balances From Nov. 29 Binance will close customer accounts in France, Spain, Italy and Poland on Dec. 31 and begin charging a monthly fee on leftover balances from Nov. 29, as the world’s largest crypto exchange still lacks a license under the European Union’s MiCA rules. A Binance spokesperson confirmed to CoinDesk the closure date over the weekend, saying the exchange is “progressively restricting certain services for affected users” now that the transition period under the Markets in Crypto-Assets framework has ended. “Affected accounts will be closed with effect from 31 December 2026,” the spokesperson said, calling it “a carefully managed process.” Binance said customer assets remain safe and accessible and described the move as “no sudden freeze.” Deposits are already blocked, but users can still withdraw crypto and fiat. Users in the four countries have shared the notices on X. The fees and deadlines According to emails that users shared, Binance will charge 0.025% of remaining crypto balances each month, or 10 USDC, whichever is higher, starting Nov. 29. The first charge lands within three days of that date, and a second follows after Dec. 24. Fees come out of USDC first and then other assets. Accounts holding less than the fee would lose the entire balance, the emails say. Anyone who withdraws everything before Nov. 29 pays nothing. Binance had not published those fee figures in a public announcement as of Sunday, so the details rest on the customer emails, not an official notice. The company’s spokesperson confirmed only the closure date and the restriction of services. The four countries share one trait: Binance ran locally registered businesses in each before the MiCA transition ended. Its first outreach to users there came in June, when it urged them to withdraw. A license Binance still has not won MiCA requires crypto firms to win authorization in one EU member state before serving customers across the bloc. Binance withdrew its Greek license application in June and said it would seek approval elsewhere, without naming the country. Reuters had reported that month that Greece’s Hellenic Capital Market Commission was poised to reject the bid, as Bitcoin Magazine reported . As the MiCA deadline arrived, the EU’s securities regulator also ordered unlicensed crypto firms to exit the market. Binance told users at the time that it remained committed to Europe. It does not appear on the European Securities and Markets Authority’s register of authorized crypto providers, and it has not said which regulator now holds its application. The closures arrive in a rough stretch for the exchange. Hackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance on Oct. 29 in a record heist the company said began with malware hidden in software downloads and fake job offers targeting engineers. item.title: NASA keeps its PROMISE to raid Mars testbeds for parts
item.description: NASA is moving ahead with its plan to repurpose a Mars rover engineering model as a lunar trundlebot for less than $400 million. The robot, dubbed PROMISE (Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration), is a cut-and-shut of engineering test articles used for the Perseverance and Curiosity rovers, currently rolling around the Red Planet. During a weekend briefing , NASA outlined the plan for PROMISE: to land the robot on the lunar surface by late 2028 for an 18-month mission. PROMISE will be preceded by NASA's VIPER trundlebot, which is expected to survive only 100 days on the Moon's surface. PROMISE will carry copies of VIPER's science instruments, including a drill capable of boring 1 meter into the lunar regolith. Power will come from a Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (RTG) left over from the Cassini mission. NASA acknowledged the fuel was processed some time ago – the Cassini mission to Saturn was launched in 1997 – but anticipates there will be plenty of heat and power for PROMISE's components. Blue Origin is to deposit the rover on the Moon. NASA awarded the company a $94 million base contract, "with an option period worth an additional $140 million based on performance to deliver PROMISE to the lunar South Pole." The figures make it difficult to ascertain the exact cost of the PROMISE mission. However, during the briefing, NASA said it had "a pretty firm agreement with JPL to basically deliver the rover to the surface under $400 million." The $400 million includes the lander, which will be Blue Origin's Mark 1. Earlier this year, The Planetary Society's chief of space policy, Casey Drier, estimated that the mission (including repurposing the hardware developed for Mars and landing it on the Moon) would cost at least $723 million. At the time, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said: "if PROMISE costs even 20 percent of your low-end estimate, we simply will not fly it." Assuming Isaacman was only talking about the rover, Drier's figure drops to $489 million without launch and landing costs. 20 percent of that is… not going to be enough. That also doesn't account for the impact of taking away the hardware built for the Mars program. During the briefing, NASA said it was "pretty comfortable" with how the Mars rovers were going and so was happy about repurposing the hardware or, as one speaker put it, "can we give it a new paint job?" A source told The Register that morale at the agency's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) was not high at present. Raiding successful programs to fulfill the administration's whims is unlikely to have improved the mood of engineers. Still. Another trundlebot on the Moon. Far better than using that spare RTG for yet another deep space mission, right? ®

item.description: For a long time, SpaceX has been synonymous with the development of newer, larger, and ever-more-reusable rockets. But that began to change over the last decade with the introduction of Starlink, and the change has accelerated during the last 18 months as the company has pivoted to data and artificial intelligence. At last week's UP.Summit conference in Florida, the vice president of launch at SpaceX, Kiko Dontchev, offered some of the most revealing comments to date about the company's changing focus, how it is embracing AI, and why the Falcon 9 rocket—which has dominated global launch for a decade and remains the world's preeminent launch vehicle—is firmly on the road to retirement. "In the last couple years, when I talk about SpaceX, yes, we are a rocket company, but fundamentally we are an infrastructure company at this point," Dontchev said. "We're building infrastructure on the ground and low Earth orbit, soon on the Moon, and obviously eventually Mars." Read full article Comments

item.title: British Comedian Russell Brand Jailed 10 Years For Rape, Assault
item.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand was Monday jailed for more than 10 years for a string of sex offences, including rape as the judge told him he had been a “sexual predator” whose fame had protected him. Brand, 51, showed no emotion as Judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with “staggering arrogance” and shown “contempt” for his victims who had suffered significant and lasting harm. Paying tribute to the “bravery” of the women who came forward, the judge told Brand he had acted “how you liked and when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live”. His wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children, slumped in her seat in the public gallery of London’s Southwark Crown Court as the total sentence of 10 years and six months was announced. Brand told his wife, who has supported him in court throughout the case, “we’ll be OK” as he was led down to the cells. The disgraced star was convicted by a jury last week of one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women between 2004 and 2009. Laura Gallacher (C), the wife of British comedian and actor Russell Brand is helped into a car after the sentencing of British comedian and TV star Russell Brand (Photo by HENRY NICHOLLS / AFP) The sentence marks the final fall in a scandal-hit showbiz career that saw him embody the anything-goes culture of 2000s British TV and radio. Brand, who has reinvented himself as an online Christian guru, held a string of prayer beads and made the sign of the cross before one of his victims personally read out her impact statement from behind a screen. The woman said she had been left “traumatised” by the assault in a London bar in 2004. “For many years, as his star was rising, it was impossible to escape seeing him all over the media, being celebrated for his disgusting behaviour against women like it was all a joke,” she told the court. Brand listened impassively, looking straight ahead. ‘Celebrated’ Russell Brand’s father ”Ron” Brand (L) leaves the court building after the sentencing of British comedian and TV star Russell Brand takes place at Southwark Crown Court in south London on November 9, 2026.(Photo by JUSTIN TALLIS / AFP) A second woman, a 21-year-old fan he raped in 2009 after they met at one of his shows, told the court she had felt she simply would “not be believed” if she reported him. “His fame, wealth and influence created a power imbalance which made me feel powerless,” she said, adding the consequences of the rape had “affected almost every aspect of my life”. The hearing came as Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the victims’ bravery would bring about wider changes to the legal system. Burnham pledged to be “relentless in making whatever improvements we can” to provide more support for victims, including setting up teams in every police force for handling rapes and serious sexual offences. item.description: Today, I’m talking with Mitch Glazier, who is CEO and chairman of the RIAA. This conversation was a real full-circle moment for me: I was in college when Napster hit, and the RIAA became everyone’s villain for suing kids for downloading music. That was when I decided to go be a copyright lawyer, which set the rest of my career in motion — and Mitch was in the background as a young lawyer at the RIAA working on those cases. So part of me was very deeply, very genuinely surprised to discover just how much fun I had talking to Mitch. That’s because here in 2026, Mitch, the RIAA, the record labels, the artists, and ordinary people are all pretty unhappy with the big AI companies in the same way, for training on everyone’s work without permission and flooding our feeds with slop. And since the RIAA is both the group that lobbies for changes to the law and also the group that files lawsuits about things that affect record labels and distributors, Mitch is a pretty busy guy these days. We got deep into the legal complexity of things like AI deepfakes, how banning them might affect other kinds of expression, and how the AI detection and labeling systems that we all seem to want might actually work in practice — especially if big platforms like Spotify and YouTube don’t get on board. I just want to get right into it. This conversation is a real ride through how AI, the law, art, and commerce might all intersect. I think you’re going to be able to tell, Mitch and I had a lot of fun talking about it. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube , where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday. Okay: RIAA CEO Mitch Glazier. Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Mitch Glazier, you’re the chairman and CEO of the Recording Industry Association of America, which people know as the RIAA. Welcome to Decoder . Thank you. Thank you, Nilay. I’m excited to be here. I am very excited to talk to you. I have to tell you, this is a very full-circle moment for me. My entire career got on track when I was in college. Napster came out, my university banned Napster from the school network, and I decided right then I was going to go be a copyright lawyer. And then I was a copyright lawyer, and I defended kids who got sued for using Kazaa . I was not good at that job. It was not fulfilling. And I became a journalist because I could write about copyright law on the iPod. So talking to you is about as full circle as it gets for me. Thank you for being on the show. Good. item.title: F1 in Brazil: You’ve got to keep your tires alive
item.description: In sports, a “ dead rubber ” is a match that takes place after the outcome of the series or championship has already been decided. The people in charge hate this*—if you wrap up a title two-thirds of the way through a season, the viewers evaporate, as there’s nothing left at stake. But anyone who decided to skip this year’s Brazilian Grand Prix this past weekend missed one of the year’s most entertaining races, as a combination of a mixed-up starting order, some very fast drivers at the back, and a wet track that dried and then saw rain again resulted in action aplenty. A peculiarity of F1 is that even if you manage to win a championship, there’s no guarantee you’ll be in a position to defend it. Take McLaren’s Lando Norris, who took the crown in 2025 after a nail-biting fight with his teammate Oscar Piastri and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen. Sadly for Lando, McLaren did not start this year in a position to win races, and even with several upgrades, the team has produced a car that is still very tricky to drive. But this weekend in Brazil, Norris demonstrated the form that earned him the number 1. Rain on Saturday during qualifying helped jumble the usual running order. It was heavy enough that drivers used the wet weather tire with deep treads, which usually generates so much spray that visibility disappears and running has to be suspended. But with fewer cars on track in the later knockout qualifying sessions, this was not a problem for once. More disruption came from grid penalties for Verstappen and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, both of whom needed to use extra power unit components outside of the season’s allowance. item.title: Microsoft's Azure Linux gets 470-plus security fixes in one almighty patching session
item.description: Microsoft has unleashed a whopper of an update for Azure Linux, packing more than 470 CVE fixes into a single release as the software industry's ever-growing pile of vulnerabilities shows little sign of shrinking. Over the weekend, Microsoft rolled out Azure Linux 3.0.2022 with fixes covering everything from the Linux kernel to open source packages and container software. The changelog runs to hundreds of entries, so anyone planning to read the whole thing might want to put the kettle on. Microsoft's release notes contain more than 470 CVE references, although some vulnerabilities appear multiple times because they affect different packages. So that's not necessarily 470 separate security holes, but it's still an impressive amount of patching for one release. The fixes span OpenSSL, curl, Kubernetes, Docker, QEMU, and a lengthy list of other packages that underpin modern Linux environments. The generic Linux kernel has been updated to version 6.6.161.1. There's also been some housekeeping following the eMudhra certificate incident , tracked as CVE-2026-114406. Microsoft has removed or distrusted root certificates that could validate compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates, while adding checks in Python and Go to reject the affected certificates. It has also preserved SSL.com TLS trust where required, presumably to avoid fixing one certificate headache by creating another. Container infrastructure gets plenty of attention, too, with fixes spanning KubeVirt, containerd, Docker Compose, and other components used to keep cloud workloads running. Several CVEs crop up repeatedly across these packages, helping explain the eye-watering number of entries in the changelog. The release includes less security-focused changes too, including new Dockerfiles, an OpenVMM patch for confidential computing support, fixes for systemd hangs, and adjustments to GRUB Secure Boot metadata. The hefty release comes amid an AI-fueled surge in vulnerability discovery that has left developers struggling to keep up with the resulting patch workload. As The Register reported e arlier today, Linux creator Linus Torvalds reckons there may finally be signs that the flood is easing, at least in some corners of the kernel. Torvalds said fixes are now arriving faster than new bug reports in the kernel's eBPF subsystem, although he noted that most other areas haven't reached that point. Whether the wider software industry is anywhere close to catching up is another matter, and Microsoft hasn't said if AI-assisted research contributed to the vulnerabilities addressed in this release. Azure Linux, formerly known as CBL-Mariner, is Microsoft's own Linux distribution, developed primarily for its cloud infrastructure and services. That makes keeping its many components patched rather more important than the modest version-number bump might suggest. And judging by the size of this latest changelog, Microsoft's patching teams aren't likely to be putting their feet up anytime soon. ®

item.title: U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too FinCEN and the Federal Reserve have formally withdrawn a 2020 proposal that would have cut the Bank Secrecy Act threshold for cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250 and spelled out that the rules cover crypto, leaving the existing $3,000 line in place. The notice, published Monday in the Federal Register, says the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the Fed’s Board of Governors “will not take further action” on a proposal they first issued on Oct. 27, 2020. That plan would have lowered the recordkeeping and Travel Rule thresholds to $250 for transfers that begin or end outside the United States. Those rules require banks and nonbank financial institutions to collect, retain and pass along customer information on transfers of $3,000 or more. It also would have clarified the meaning of “money” in both rules so they apply to transactions involving convertible virtual currency, along with digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. Why the agencies backed off Per the notcie, FinCEN and the Fed received nearly 3,000 comments on the proposal, most of them substantially similar form letters. Commenters generally opposed the lower threshold, arguing that it would burden smaller institutions and could push consumers sending remittances toward less regulated channels. Many also noted that potentially illicit transfers below $3,000 were already being flagged to FinCEN through suspicious activity reports. Several said the threshold should rise instead, citing inflation since 1995. Sentiment on the crypto language was mixed. Companies that provide crypto services and their trade groups opposed it, citing technical limits and the lack of an international messaging standard for crypto transfers, while some banks and money services businesses supported it. The agencies gave two reasons for pulling the proposal. More than five years have passed, and they said more public feedback would help before adopting anything similar. The withdrawal, they wrote, gives the public “certainty” that no final rule will be issued without another chance to comment. The second reason is the crypto industry itself. The notice says crypto markets “have continued to mature” and new legal frameworks are emerging, citing the GENIUS Act stablecoin law enacted on July 18, 2025. Any future change tied to crypto, the agencies said, should be considered in light of those developments so it is “fit for purpose.” What the withdrawal does and does not do The notice does not repeal or amend any rule. The $3,000 threshold that has applied for decades stays where it is, and so does the existing Travel Rule. What disappears is the specific path to $250 and the proposed wording that would have written crypto into the definition of money. The agencies did not say whether they plan a new proposal or offer a timeline. The withdrawal is the latest in a run of reversals from Treasury. On Oct.

item.title: Futuristic aircraft takes flight at NASA | Space photo of the day for Nov. 9, 2026
item.description: null The future of flight meets space exploration as a futuristic electric aircraft hovers beside Blue Origin's massive New Glenn rocket stage. (Image credit: Chelsea Gohd/Future) A futuristic single-person aircraft takes to the skies at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, with the upper stage of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket providing a dramatic backdrop. The unusual scene was captured during the MAX POWER event, which brought together innovators and emerging technologies at the iconic spaceflight facility. What is it? The photograph shows a single-person electric aircraft called Jetson ONE, developed by Jetson, a Swedish startup company working to bring personal flight to the skies. The compact rotorcraft uses multiple propellers to climb into the air, allowing it to take off and vertically without the need for a runway. The aircraft was performing flight demonstrations during the UP.Summit gathering, which formed part of the larger MAX POWER event at the Kennedy Space Center. During the demonstrations, the Jetson ONE demonstrated its ability to maneuver through the air and hover in place, giving spectators a close-up look at the technology in action. Jetson ONE demonstration at MAX POWER. (Image credit: Chelsea Gohd/Future) Why is it amazing? The photograph offers a fascinating glimpse at two very different approaches to flight. While Jetson is developing small electric aircraft designed for personal transportation, Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket is built to carry payloads far beyond Earth's atmosphere.

item.title: How to shop like a pro during Black Friday and Cyber Monday
item.description: Despite Amazon and other retailers filling the summer and fall months with more sales than ever before, Black Friday and Cyber Monday remain the biggest shopping days of the year. And, in recent years, the sale periods have started earlier, giving you more time to take advantage of the deals. We’re already hard at work to find the best prices on phones, accessories, 4K TVs, noise-canceling headphones, gaming gear, and other tech throughout the deal-packed weeks culminating in the big events, whether you plan to shop in person or online. You can always count on us to publish only the best deals that you need to know about , no matter the season. However, if you want to be among the first people to spot price drops on the products you’re interested in, you’ll want to get a head start on your Black Friday and Cyber Monday game plan. Thankfully, we have a few suggestions for scouting early sales at your favorite retailers, finding the right price-tracking tool, and setting up email alerts to ensure you don’t miss rare discounts at Amazon and elsewhere. Leverage a price-tracking tool or deal aggregator The most effective way to find a truly great deal is to set up a price-tracking tool. We’ve included a few of our favorites below, many of which we use daily here at The Verge . Each can help you track deals at various retailers — including Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and Target — but they each do so differently and come with their own set of advantages / disadvantages. All of them are free to use, and once you’ve added the products you’re interested in keeping an eye on, you can rest easy knowing that you don’t need to take any action until it comes time to make a purchase. Just make sure you keep your email notifications on so you see the alerts as they come in. CamelCamelCamel CamelCamelCamel is arguably the most popular price-tracking tool at The Verge , and for good reason: it’s incredibly useful since it tracks the price of every product sold on Amazon and can send you alerts when an item falls to a customizable price threshold. Once a product reaches the desired price you’ve set (or lower), you’ll get an email about it. You can use the extension’s price graph to determine what price is likely to happen based on historical data, but it’s always a shot in the dark. To track prices and get alerts via email, you’ll need to create a free CamelCamelCamel account. Additionally, we suggest installing the site’s browser extension , The Camelizer, which works with Google Chrome, Safari, Mozilla Firefox, Opera, and Microsoft Edge. The handy tool lets you view pricing trends on a product-by-product basis and set your desired price without leaving Amazon. It’s fantastic, easy to use, and works in several countries, including the US, UK, Canada, Germany, Spain, France, Italy, and Australia. As mentioned, the tracker only works for products listed on Amazon. However, in May, the company released CamelMart , its price tracker for Walmart. While it doesn’t have a

item.title: Here are the price-matching policies for Best Buy, Walmart, and others
item.description: Nothing is more frustrating than buying a new pair of headphones or an OLED TV, only to find out you could have gotten it cheaper somewhere else a few days or weeks later. That’s why, to keep customers happy and prevent them from shopping elsewhere, some retailers offer price-matching policies that promise to match a lower price found elsewhere. That kind of information comes in handy year-round, but it’s especially helpful during the weeks of deals leading up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Below are the price-matching policies for several major retailers. A few things to note: First, each retailer has its own set of rules and restrictions. We’ve summarized some of them here, but we recommend visiting the provided links and reading the policies carefully. Second, most retailers that serve as marketplaces for other sellers, including wholesale retailers like Costco, don’t offer protections, and many traditional stores won’t match their prices. Lastly, there are always exceptions to the rules. If you’re looking for a deal on a product and you know it’s available for a lower price elsewhere (or it was previously offered at the same retailer), it never hurts to call or chat with a customer service rep and ask if they’ll match the price. You have nothing to lose but time, and there’s always a chance they may find a loophole or make a special exception. Amazon Amazon doesn’t offer price matching. Full stop. You can contact customer support, but even if you’re an Amazon Prime customer, they likely won’t help. That said, the online retailer does offer a liberal return policy , meaning you can often return an item you purchased from Amazon if it’s available for less elsewhere (or at Amazon). Then, you can just repurchase the product wherever it’s cheapest. Target Target used to let shoppers price match identical items sold by select retailers, including Amazon, but no longer does so. Under its current policy, shoppers can only request a price adjustment if they find an identical qualifying item for less than they paid on Target.com, at their local Target store, or through an eligible Target Circle deal. Target will also price match Target Plus Partner (the retailer’s name for third-party sellers) items if the same Target Plus Partner on Target.com has it for less, or with a Target Circle deal. Price matches can be requested at the time of purchase or within 14 days after purchase. For the 2026 holiday season, Target has extended the aforementioned price-match window. If you purchase an eligible item between November 1st and December 24th, you can request a price adjustment if its price drops at Target during that period. The extended policy also applies to eligible Target Plus Partner purchases. To request a price match, you’ll need to show the online price or digital version of the ad and provide your original receipt or packing slip; screenshots and photos aren’t accepted. item.title: Here’s when the Black Friday sales start at Walmart, Target, and other retailers
item.description: Black Friday officially kicks off on November 27th, but if you plan to make that the only day you buy gifts this holiday season, you’re missing out. Several prominent retailers, including Best Buy and Walmart, are preparing to roll out their holiday discounts both in-store and online. Best Buy is even offering price protection through the holiday shopping season on select goods, so if you buy early and the same item drops in price, you can get the better deal retroactively. That being said, it’s important to know how every major retailer is handling the shopping event this year, whether you plan to take advantage of the slew of early holiday deals or hold off until the day after Thanksgiving. If you plan to spend some cash, here are the schedules and expectations for Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and all the major retailers we know of. Amazon Amazon has yet to announce its full Black Friday playbook, but the online retailer has dropped a few early deals in its so-called Holiday Shop , including steep discounts on Sony’s WH-1000XM6 headphones, the Google Pixel 11 Pro XL , and fitness trackers like the Fitbit Inspire 3 . Just be aware that Amazon does not offer price matching, so price “protection” for many Amazon shoppers means buying the item at the lower price point and returning the original — which, unfortunately, is pretty wasteful. Walmart Like in previous years, Walmart plans to roll out its Black Friday deals in three distinct waves. The first runs from November 12th through November 15th, starting online at 12:01AM ET and in stores at 6AM local time. Walmart Plus members will also get early access to some deals beginning at 12:01AM ET on November 12th, with the sale opening up to everyone at 12:01AM ET on November 13th. Walmart’s official Black Friday sale then kicks off at 12:01AM on Monday, November 23rd, with Walmart Plus members once again getting early access to select deals online. Whatever “hot Deal drops” remain will then be available to non-members at 12:01AM ET on November 24th. Walmart’s in-store Black Friday sale will then kick off at 6AM local time on November 27th. The retailer’s Cyber Monday sale, meanwhile, will kick off online at 12:01AM ET on November 30th and run through December 2nd. The retailer hasn’t shared many deal specifics yet, but did offer a sneak peek in a recent press release promising discounts across a range of categories, including toys, fashion, beauty, and home goods. Best Buy Best Buy officially kicked off its Black Friday promos on October 30th, with the retailer launching its first set of doorbuster deals on Halloween. Like last year, Best Buy will drop subsequent deals every Friday in the run-up to the holidays, and those who sign up for My Best Buy Plus or My Best Buy Total will also get up to $25 in bonus rewards during select doorbuster events. As for Best Buy’s main Black Friday event, the promos are slated to begin on November 19th and run for 10 days. The retailer will then hold its Cyber Sunday

item.title: Here are the shipping and return policies for all the big-name retailers
item.description: With the holidays quickly appro aching, everyone will soon be on the hunt for gifts and the fastest way to get them. Thankfully, many retailers offer generous shipping policies, with some even providing free two-day shipping or same-day delivery if you’re willing to pay a little extra. And just in case the gift you choose isn’t quite right, many retailers offer extended return policies so your giftee can get something more to their liking. For your convenience, we’ve compiled the current shipping and return policies for all the big-name retailers, from Amazon to Walmart. A few already have holiday policies in place, but we’ll be keeping tabs on them and updating our list accordingly. Hopefully, knowing more about how much leeway you have to make a return will help lessen that inevitable holiday angst (fingers crossed). Amazon Shipping : Same-day delivery is not available on Thanksgiving, Christmas, or New Year’s (it’s also limited on Black Friday). However, Prime members get free same-day delivery on qualifying orders in qualifying ZIP codes provided they meet the “minimum qualifying dollar threshold” ( which varies by location) of eligible items in their cart. One-Day and Two-Day Delivery with no minimum purchase amount required is also available to Prime members for qualifying products. Non-Prime buyers will find shipping options on the order page of each specific product. Returns : As part of its holiday promotional period, Amazon says most items purchased between November 1st and December 31st can be returned until January 31st, 2027. Apple products, however, must be returned by January 15th, 2027. Note that this policy applies to both Prime and non-Prime buyers. Apple Shipping : Apple has yet to provide details on its holiday shipping policy; however, last year, it offered free delivery of in-stock items that hadn’t been engraved by Christmas Eve if you ordered before 9PM ET on December 21st. Apple also offers free next-day or two-hour delivery from local stores in most metro areas for an additional fee, or you can opt to pick up purchases yourself by visiting your local Apple Store. Returns : Apple is offering an extended return period for online orders received between November 6th and December 25th, allowing you to return items until January 8th, 2027. Purchases made after December 25th are generally subject to the usual terms and conditions, and must be returned within 14 calendar days of your initial purchase date. Target Shipping : Target offers free two-day shipping on many orders if you spend $35 or more or use your Target Circle Card . Same-day delivery costs $9.99 per order, but it’s included with a Target Circle 360 membership ($10.99 a month / $99 a year). Your mileage may vary for same-day delivery availability based on the item and your location. Returns : Target offers an extended return policy for electronics and entertainment items purchased between November 1st and December 24th, allowing you to return them until January 24

item.title: Youth Olympics: Nwankwo, Bright Win Historic Gold In Men’s, Women’s 100m
item.description: Nigeria made an impressive start to the athletics competition at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Sunday, winning gold in both the men’s and women’s 100m finals at the Complexe Iba Mar Diop. Rosemary Nwankwo opened the country’s gold-medal account in the women’s 100m, crossing the finish line in 11.16 seconds to claim victory and set a new personal best. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, gold medalist (C), Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates (L), silver medalist, and Dana Salem of Qatar (R), bronze medalist, pose on the podium after the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) She finished ahead of Arwa Ali of the United Arab Emirates, who clocked 11.41 seconds, also a personal best, while Dana Salem of Qatar settled for bronze in 11.48 seconds. The win made Nwankwo the third Nigerian woman to take Youth Olympic 100m gold, following Josephine Omaka at the inaugural Singapore 2010 Games and Rosemary Chukwuma at Buenos Aires 2018. Nigeria’s Rosemary Nwankwo, winner of the women’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, poses next to the board at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) Nigeria’s celebrations continued minutes later as Gift Bright secured another gold medal in the men’s 100m, finishing in a personal-best time of 10.28 seconds. China’s Zhang Hangyu came second in 10.57 seconds, while Poland’s Szymon Dolega claimed bronze in 10.61 seconds. Speaking after her triumph, Nwankwo said she remained focused on her race despite the significance of the occasion. Nigeria’s Gift Bright, react after winning the men’s 100-meter semifinal at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) “There was no pressure on me. I run my race. I focused on me, and I did it,” she said. “I’ve prayed for this moment, and I did it.” For Bright, the victory was particularly significant after a thigh injury had troubled him in the two weeks leading up to the competition. China’s Hangyu Zhang (L), silver medalist; Nigeria’s Gift Bright (C), gold medalist; and Poland’s Szymon Dolega (R), bronze medalist, pose on the podium after the men’s 100-meter track and field final at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, held at the Iba Mar Diop Complex (CID Stadium) in Dakar on November 8, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS REMENE / AFP) He admitted that the injury had affected his confidence but said he was relieved to compete without pain in the final. “I want to tell you guys that at the next (Youth) Olympics, expect Nigeria to win it again. We are good sprinters,” he said. We know how to condition ourselves to stay where we are. It’s a very big thing for us.” The post Youth Olympics: Nwankwo, Bright Win Historic Gold In Men’s, Women’s 100m appeared first on

item.title: Obi Alleges NFF Blocked Him From Greeting Victorious Flamingos
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi has alleged that officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) prevented him from greeting members of the national Under-17 women’s football team, the Flamingos, following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Obi said he was allegedly informed that the officials had warned against allowing him to approach the players, allegedly threatening that they would lose their jobs if he did. The former Anambra State governor disclosed this in a statement posted on his official X handle on Monday, after the Flamingos returned to Nigeria following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Morocco. Obi said he arrived at the airport at about 7 a.m. on Monday to board a flight to Enugu when he sighted the victorious team preparing to leave the airport. Flamingos arriving in Nigeria. He said he subsequently asked his protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether he could greet and welcome the players. “With genuine joy and enthusiasm, I asked my Protocol Officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether I could greet and welcome the team. I was informed that officials of the Nigerian Football Federation (NFF) had refused and had requested that I not approach them because, if I did, they would all lose their jobs,” he wrote. Obi described the incident as another example of what he called the growing culture of “toxic politics” in Nigeria, alleging that he had experienced similar treatment during a previous visit to a football event. He recounted that on March 25, 2025, he travelled to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, for a World Cup qualifying match, where he said the governor received him at the VIP stand. According to him, after the match, other government officials were allowed to greet the players, but he was again prevented from doing so. “Following the match, other government officials went to greet the players, but I was again prevented from doing so. I was told by the officials that they would lose their jobs if I proceeded,” he said. The former governor expressed concern over what he described as the increasing politicisation of public engagements, arguing that political differences should not prevent Nigerians from celebrating national achievements. “It is deeply troubling to witness the extent of toxic politics into which our nation has descended since 2025. Each year appears to bring further deterioration. This reflects how deeply Nigeria has been affected. “The new Nigeria we aspire to build must have no room for hostility, intimidation, or discrimination, regardless of political affiliation. It must be a Nigeria in which unity, mutual respect, and our shared humanity take,” he said. U-17 World Cup Victory Flamingos celebrating their U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team, the Flamingos, made history by defeating Japan 2-1 to become the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. item.title: SpaceX will launch epic double-catch Starship Flight 15 test mission on Nov. 13
item.description: null SpaceX will make spaceflight history this week, if all goes according to plan. The company announced over the weekend that it's targeting Friday (Nov. 13) for the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket, which will attempt something that's never been done before. "The upcoming flight is planned to be the first to return both Starship and Super Heavy to the launch site for catch," SpaceX wrote in a description of Flight 15 . "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket." SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 14th test flight on Sept. 28, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Super Heavy is Starship's giant booster, and Starship (or Ship for short) is its upper-stage spacecraft. As SpaceX's description noted, both elements are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable. "Catch" refers to SpaceX's recovery mechanism for both stages: Each will return to the launch mount at SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas and be plucked out of the sky by the tower's "chopstick" arms. SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three Starship flights to date, but it has never tried the maneuver with Ship. It's a taller order; Ship flies higher and farther than Super Heavy, so its return to Earth is more complex and energetic. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk already told us that Flight 15 would likely feature a double-catch attempt . But the newly released mission description gives us a launch date, as well as details about the flight. Starship Die Cast Rocket Model Was $47.99 Now $39.99 on Amazon . Even if you can't see SpaceX's Starship in person, you can score a model of your own. Standing at 13.77 inches (35 cm), this is a 1:375 ratio of SpaceX's Starship as a desktop model. The materials here are alloy steel and it weighs just 225g. View Deal Flight 15 is scheduled to launch from Starbase on Friday during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). Super Heavy will come back to Starbase for its tower catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff, if all goes to plan. But Ship will stay up quite a bit longer. The upper stage will go orbital, something Starship did for the first time on Flight 14 on Sept. 28. And, as on Flight 14, Ship will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites, the vanguard of a new megaconstellation that will eventually consist of about 100,000 spacecraft , according to Musk. Composite photo showing the Super Heavy booster of SpaceX's Starship megarocket coming in for a landing on the launch mount during the vehicle's fifth-ever test flight, on Oct. 13, 2024.
