item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 probe bounces back from communications glitch in interstellar space
item.description: null Voyager, 1, humanity's most distant spacecraft, is back in contact after briefly losing touch with Earth last month. The spacecraft stopped phoning home for about 48 hours between Oct. 18 and 20 due to a communications glitch that Voyager 1 resolved on its own, before engineers could send the long-running spacecraft a remote fix. "This is the first time we've seen the spacecraft do something like this, but we are also at a point in the mission where we have to expect the unexpected," Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), said in an agency statement about the incident on Oct. 29. Voyager 1 is almost one light-day from Earth, meaning that a command takes nearly a day to reach the spacecraft and a response takes another day to come back to our planet. The spacecraft will reach the light-day milestone on Nov. 18, at 16.09 billion miles (25.89 billion kilometers) from Earth. NASA's Deep Space Network of three antennas does check-ins to make sure the spacecraft is doing well. On Oct. 18 and 19, Voyager 1 did not respond. Its signal fortunately reappeared on Oct. 20. "Engineers still are investigating what caused the communication loss," JPL added in the statement, but said it appears Voyager 1 went into a sort of safe mode. "The team has so far determined that one group of thrusters went offline and their backups turned on. Such a swap is programmed to occur automatically if the spacecraft computers detect something amiss with the active thrusters." Voyager 1 and its still-operational twin, Voyager 2 , both launched in 1977 on an initial mission to explore planets in the solar system. The two spacecraft took advantage of a rare alignment that allowed them to swing from Jupiter to Saturn to Uranus and Neptune using a minimum of fuel, although funding to explore the more distant planets and moons was not guaranteed at launch. The spacecraft duly swung by Jupiter's and Saturn's systems (some months apart from each other) to great acclaim before parting pathways. Voyager 1's close-up view of Saturn's rings as well as the moon Titan — which may have prebiotic or pre-life chemistry — altered the spacecraft's trajectory to put it high above the plane of the solar system. Meanwhile, Voyager 2 flew on to Uranus and Neptune in 1986 and 1989, respectively, providing the only up-close view of these planetary systems to date. An image of Saturn taken by Voyager 1 on Nov. 16, 1980, four days after the spacecraft flew past the planet. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Running on nuclear power, and continuing to deliver valuable science from deep space, the Voyagers saw their missions extended repeatedly. Both crossed into interstellar space a few years ago, and are still operational. But with age comes a cost: the plutonium power sources on both spacecraft are diminishing, requiring engineers to periodically shut off instruments or come up with other clever ways of saving power. item.title: Earth photobombs spacewalking Canadian astronaut | Space photo of the day for Nov. 5, 2026
item.description: null Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk poses for a photo during his spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026. (Image credit: CSA) Spacewalks are hard work, so sometimes you need to take a break for a moment and snap a gorgeous selfie with your home planet in the background. What is it? During a pre-Halloween spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk took a moment to pose for a photograph. In this moment , the International Space Station to which he was tethered was orbiting 267 miles (430 kilometers) above the South Atlantic Ocean down below on Earth. During this spacewalk — the first for a Canadian since 2019 — Kutryk and NASA astronaut Anil Menon worked together to install a new roll-out solar array on the station while also performing some "get ahead" tasks to prep for the next spacewalk, which is happening today (Nov. 5). During today's excursion, the same two astronauts will venture out into space, tethered to the space station, to install the eighth and final roll-out solar array. These eight new arrays will boost the station's available power by a total of 30%, according to NASA officials. Why is it incredible? When we think of astronauts working in space, we might think of the important science and research they're doing aboard the station. Astronauts work on everything from biomedical research to plant science and physics experiments. But the job also includes work on the space station itself. Sometimes they have to venture out into the vacuum of space to fix urgent problems. These situations can be tense, and there's a lot of pressure to get things absolutely right. But even spacewalks that do relatively mundane maintenance work, like the one on Oct. 29, come with pressure. Every minute that astronauts spend outside of the space station, there are countless risk factors floating around. Earth orbit is a very harsh environment, after all, even if it does allow for some pretty amazing selfies.

item.title: NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins is the 1st Black woman to command a space mission. Will we see more diversity in the future on the final frontier?
item.description: null When Jessica Watkins became commander of her mission to the International Space Station, she didn't just fulfill her duty as an astronaut — she made history. Watkins is commanding SpaceX's Crew-13 mission , which launched her and three other astronauts to the I nternational Space Station on Oct. 1. As their Crew Dragon capsule lifted off atop a Falcon 9 rocket that day, Watkins became the first Black woman to command a crewed mission to space. Spaceflight and space science are historically white and male-dominated fields, so this milestone carries incredible significance. "This is certainly an important milestone, I think both for our agency and for the country," Watkins said in a press briefing ahead of Crew-13's launch. This is Watkins' second spaceflight. She previously flew on SpaceX's Crew-4 mission in 2022 and has spent more than 200 days in space to date, though that number will keep climbing for a while, as Crew-13 is set to be an approximately six-month mission. A geologist, astronaut, aquanaut and former professional rugby player, Watkins brings an incredible variety of skills to her new role as mission commander. And, in addition to what she's bringing to her colleagues on mission, she's also providing some serious inspiration for those back on Earth. NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins floats in the International Space Station’s cupola during the Crew-4 mission in this photo, which NASA shared on May 9, 2022. (Image credit: NASA) "Jessica is an inspirational symbol to a lot of people," commercial astronaut and fellow geologist Sian Proctor , who became the first Black woman to pilot a spacecraft on SpaceX's private Inspiration4 mission to orbit in September 2021, told Space.com . Sian shared that the two even crossed paths years ago, when their astronaut training aligned. "It just means so much to so many people when you see a diverse crew, and particularly women, and women of color, in leadership positions," Proctor said. "And it means something for America." The visibility of Watkins' accomplishments and missions carries significant cultural weight. However, in addition to recognizing her many achievements, "you also should celebrate the fact that she's African American and a role model for her community," Proctor said. Sian Proctor from aboard the SpaceX Dragon capsule during the Inspiration4 mission. (Image credit: Tripadvisor) Proctor, who similarly made spaceflight history with her mission, sees Watkins' role in Crew-13 as potentially more than just an exciting moment. Hopefully, she said, it will help lay the foundation for a more diverse future in human spaceflight . "When they announced Jessica, I was super excited because it shows progress," Proctor said, sharing that she finds incredible importance in the "idea of looking at your crew and recognizing the fact that diversity makes the crew stronger." item.title: NASA announces experimental X-70 Fractal aircraft: A 'new beginning for aeronautics'
item.description: null NASA has revealed a glimpse of its next X-plane, known as the X-70 Fractal. Or at least what it thinks the X-70 will look like once built. The agency released a short statement on Wednesday (Nov. 4) announcing the X-plane , or experimental plane, declaring it to be a highly maneuverable test bed with a "rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology," allowing NASA to swap both external and internal components on-the-fly. This modular architecture will allow NASA to "explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight," according to the agency's statement . The announcement was made alongside an AI-generated image showing two canted vertical tail fins emerging from swirling smoke. Little can be gleaned from the image about what final form the X-70 might take, but the tail fins are somewhat reminiscent of the Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor or Boeing F/A-18 Super Hornet . "The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in the statement. The NASA chief called the aircraft "just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics" and said that the agency expects the X-70 to make its first flight within two years. "This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly," Isaacman added. NASA's statement fleshes out a few details about the X-70's capabilities. According to the agency, Fractal will fly at a cruise speed of Mach .75, about the same as a Boeing 737 Classic. The X-70 will be able to reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet (13.7 kilometers), and will have a range exceeding 1,726 miles (2,777 kilometers, or 1,500 nautical miles). The X-70 Fractal will also be able to carry around 2,000 pounds (900 kg) of experimental payloads both internally and externally, which will allow for a "wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities," NASA said in the statement. NASA adds it will have a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds (4,535 kilograms), around the same weight as the Scaled Composites- and Northrop Grumman-developed Model 437 Vanguard experimental aircraft. In fact, the two aircraft share a similar silhouette — at least in the AI image of the X-70 Fractal NASA has released so far. Scaled Composites' Model 437 Vanguard experimental aircraft (top); NASA's render of its upcoming X-70 Fractal (bottom). (Image credit: Northrop Grumman/NASA) The agency's most recent X-plane, the X-59 , has been flying for over a year. That jet features a radical long-nosed geometry without a forward windscreen; pilots fly by way of an augmented reality screen that combines views from sensors and a forward-facing camera. That geometry dampens the shockwaves coming off of the X-59 when it flies faster than the sound barrier, allowing it to fly at speeds over Mach 1 without the thunderous sonic booms that typically accompany supersonic flight. item.title: China lays out plans to land astronauts on the moon 'before 2030.' Can NASA still win this race?
item.description: null China has given us some details about the epic moon landing it plans to pull off a few years from now. Chinese officials laid out the roadmap for its crewed lunar campaign at the 7th Manned Space Symposium, which was held Oct. 31 and Nov. 1 in Beijing. The campaign consists of four missions, culminating in a crewed touchdown "before 2030," according to media reports . That timeline — which is consistent with previous statements made by the China Manned Space Agency — keeps the pressure on the U.S., which aims to put its own astronauts down on the moon in 2028, via NASA's Artemis program . Leaked slide confirms the four-mission progression toward China’s crewed lunar landing:🚀2027: Maiden flight of Long March 10A carrying Mengzhou CSS cargo resupply mission, to validate the new human-rated vehicle and Mengzhou’s orbital operations in LEO.🚀2028: First flight of the heavier CZ-10 with an uncrewed Lanyue lander performing a lunar descent and ascent test, exercising the lander’s propulsion and guidance.🚀🚀2029: Dual CZ-10 launches of Mengzhou and Lanyue for a full-scale lunar-orbit rehearsal, demonstrating rendezvous, docking, and integrated operations.🚀🚀Before the end of 2030: Dual CZ-10 crewed lunar landing mission. November 1, 2026 China shooting for the moon The first mission in China's four-part lunar campaign is scheduled to fly in 2027, according to CNSpaceflight , an X account that keeps a close eye on China's activities in space. The outlet cited an X user who shared a presentation slide of the plan. That launch — the first of of China's new Long March 10A rocket — will send an uncrewed Mengzhou spacecraft to low Earth orbit (LEO) for a series of tests. Mengzhou , whose name means "Dream Vessel," is the next-gen crew capsule that will carry Chinese astronauts to lunar orbit. Mission number two, launching in 2028, will involve a different set of hardware — the more powerful Long March 10 rocket and the Lanyue ("Embracing the Moon") lunar lander. This will also be an uncrewed flight, and it will mark the debut of the Long March 10, which will send Lanyue to orbit around the moon. If all goes to plan, Lanyue will touch down on the moon and then launch itself back to lunar orbit. Mission number three, flying in 2029, will also target an uncrewed lunar landing, but it will feature two Long March 10 launches — one apiece for Mengzhou and Lanyue. The two spacecraft will conduct a rendezvous and docking rehearsal in lunar orbit, then separate for Lanyue's trip down to the surface. This will set the stage for mission four — the real deal, in which two Long March 10s launch a crewed Mengzhou and an uncrewed Lanyue "before 2030." The two vessels will dock in lunar orbit, and the astronauts will move into Lanyue for their historic lunar landing. Three astronauts will apparently launch on Mengzhou, and two of them will land on the moon aboard Lanyue, according to CNSpaceflight . The duo will spend three days on the lunar surface, conducting moonwalks

item.title: U.S. Consulate General Highlights Fashion’s Role in Expanding U.S.-Nigeria Commercial Ties During Lagos Fashion Week
item.description: U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth delivering remarks at the event hosted at the Consul General’s residence in Lagos. Consulate General Lagos recently recognized the contributions of Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele at a lunch held at the height of Lagos Fashion Week 2026. The event recognized Akerele’s vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. The occasion brought together designers, entrepreneurs, and creative leaders to highlight fashion’s role in strengthening U.S.-Nigeria ties. “It’s an honor to celebrate Lagos Fashion Week 2026 with so many of Nigeria’s most talented designers and creative leaders. For 15 years, Omoyemi has built one of Africa’s premier fashion showcases, connecting Nigerian designers with American buyers and retailers and showing how trade creates opportunity for both our countries,” said U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth . In attendance was also award-winning American-born actress and producer Osas Ighodaro . Guests also experienced a new fashion themed game developed by Lagos based Maliyo Games, highlighting fashion’s growing links with technology and entertainment. Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele speaking at the event hosted by the U.S. Consul General in her honor, celebrating her vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. Fashion is a major global industry, supporting jobs and commercial activity across design, retail, and related sectors including in both the United States and Nigeria. U.S. consumers spent an estimated $560 billion on clothing and footwear in 2025, according to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis. For Nigeria’s fashion industry, access to the American market offers a pathway to expand the reach of Nigerian designers while offering entry points into Africa for U.S. retailers and businesses. Since founding Lagos Fashion Week in 2011, Omoyemi Akerele has built the platform into one of Africa’s leading fashion showcases. Its 2025 edition featured more than 60 designers and welcomed approximately 15,000 guests. Lagos Fashion Week (LFW) has also become a bridge to the American fashion industry. Leading American singer Ciara walked the LFW runway in 2025, while Studio 189, the label co-founded by American actress Rosario Dawson , has shown collections in Lagos. New York-based Nigerian designer Tia Adeola has also featured her collections at LFW as well as American media outlets including Vogue and Essence being among the leading U.S. outlets that have covered the shows. LFW helps Nigerian designers explore the U.S. market through trade shows such as Coterie and NYNOW in New York and Liberty Fairs in Miami. item.title: 2 astronauts will finish upgrading ISS solar arrays during spacewalk today: Watch it live
item.description: null Two spacewalking astronauts will finish upgrading the International Space Station's power system today (Nov. 5), and you can watch the action live. NASA astronaut Anil Menon and the Canadian Space Agency 's Joshua Kutryk will install the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) today, during a roughly seven-hour spacewalk that's scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com , courtesy of NASA, beginning at 7 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT). NASA astronaut Anil Menon points his camera toward his spacesuit’s helmet visor and takes a selfie during a spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) Today's extravehicular activity (EVA) will be the second in a week for Menon and Kutryk, who installed the station's seventh iROSA during an Oct. 29 spacewalk . That excursion was the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the ISS to date, and the first EVA for a Canadian astronaut since 2019. Today's spacewalk will wrap up an ambitious ISS power upgrade that has taken more than five years to pull off. "The installation job will complete the years-long process that began in June 2021 to augment the space station’s power generating capacity from 160 kilowatts to about 215 kilowatts," NASA officials wrote about the EVA in a blog post on Tuesday (Nov. 3) . That's a boost of about 30%. Menon and Kutryk are currently sharing the ISS with five other astronauts — NASA's Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov. Delaney, Kutryk, Teteryatnikov and Watkins arrived at the ISS on Oct. 1, on SpaceX's Crew-13 mission . Dubrov, Kikina and Menon got there in mid-July, aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft.

item.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
item.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
item.description: null On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms. After failing to launch this batch of cubesats, the Super Strypi program never recovered from its failure, and the Air Force never tried launching another one. The U.S. Air Force’s rail-launched Super Strypi rocket lifted off from Hawaii about 9:45 p.m. local time on Nov. 3, 2015,, roared toward the sky and failed less than a minute into the long-awaited flight. (Image credit: U.S. Air Force) Why it mattered The Super Strypi rocket was a 21st century take on a 1960s rocket. It was designed to be a modern version of the three-stage Strypi sounding rocket used for for reentry vehicle and anti-missile target tests. Its three stages, powered by Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, was designed to reach orbit, rather than suborbital trajectories common to most sounding rockets. The U.S. Air Force hoped Super Strypi would be a new tool for quick-response launches based on national security needs. Altogether, it was designed to launch small payloads of up to 300 kilograms into space for a mere $15 million per mission . The rocket's primary payload was the ORS-4 satellite, short for Operationally Responsive Space 4, which was built for the Air Force by engineers at the University of Hawaii (who nicknamed it HiakaSat). It was designed to capture Earth imagery and monitor the environment over the course of a year. The 12 other payloads on Super Strypi included eight cubesats for NASA's Edison Demonstration of Smallsat Networks mission, and as well as four others for universities that had been added as secondary payloads. Since the Super Strypi failure, neither the Air Force or Space Force has opted to use the rocket for a new mission. The Space Force has turned instead to commercial companies for fast-turnaround launch support. In June of this year, the U.S. Space Force teamed up with Rocket Lab to launch the Victus Haze mission with just 17 hours of notice , a new record to demonstrate short-turnaround launch response. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Trump declares 'American space superiority for all eternity' in election night proclamation
item.description: null President Trump issued a declaration yesterday (Nov. 3), proclaiming space open to all humanity for exploration, and the right of American citizens to develop and settle the solar system according to United States laws. "The American Declaration of Freedom in Space," describes space as the "province of all humans" and asserts that the United States will lead humanity's expansion into the cosmos. The proclamation reiterates the administration's goals with NASA's Artemis program to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 and eventually sending astronauts to Mars , but introduces no new funding, programs or policy directives. "Our Nation will lead the way in the exploration, development, use, and settlement of these new frontiers — forging an interplanetary civilization founded on the enduring and inalienable rights of freedom and individual liberty," the document says. Trump invoked America's "frontier spirit," highlighting Apollo 11 astronauts as the first people in history to walk on the moon's surface and robotic rovers exploring Mars as examples of U.S. leadership, and emphasized the country's flourishing commercial space sector helping ensure "American space superiority for all eternity." "The nation that leads in space will shape the future of humanity," the declaration says, and pledges that America will carry the values of faith, freedom and individual liberty into an interplanetary civilization. The proclamation also highlights the success of NASA's Artemis II mission in April, which carried four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon and set a record for the farthest humans have ever traveled from Earth . The follow-up to that mission, Artemis III, is scheduled to launch next summer (2027), and will test rendezvous and docking operations between NASA's Orion spacecraft and the program's two commercial lunar landers in low Earth orbit . Artemis IV will be the program's first lunar landing mission, and is targeted for 2028. A December 2025 executive order from the President reaffirmed the goal of meeting that timeline, as well as the deployment of the initial elements for a permanent lunar outpost by 2030. Trump's declaration yesterday does not establish new NASA programs, allocate additional funding or issue instructions to federal agencies. Its sweeping language, though, does echo some of the principles in the 1967 Outer Space Treaty , which guarantees freedom of exploration while prohibiting national sovereignty claims on other planets.

item.title: Upcoming Marvel movies and TV shows: Avengers: Doomsday, Secret Wars, X-Men & more
item.description: Marvel fatigue? Think again, especially after Spider-Man: Brand New Day made over $2.5 billion worldwide and Avengers: Doomsday is looking hot, hot, hot! But even after the uneven Multiverse Saga ends (hopefully on a high note), Marvel Studios won’t be stopping. So, we've put together a list of all the upcoming MCU movies and shows confirmed so far. While the MCU isn't stopping, Marvel has slowed its roll, with the powers that be returning to the “quality over quantity” approach that defined Marvel Studios’ Infinity Saga output. This means no more than three movies per year and, perhaps more importantly, severely cutting down on TV productions, with a focus on multi-season shows rather than limited series that should’ve been a movie. It’s a time of change for both Disney and Marvel, but it seems everyone agrees the big screen reigns supreme, so expect a thinner streaming output and more relevant movies starring characters you actually know. More will be revealed in due time, but for now, here’s what lies at the Multiverse Saga’s end and beyond... Spoilers ahead for the Marvel Cinematic Universe so far. item.title: 'Trials and Tribble-ations' at 30: The classic 'Star Trek: Deep Space Nine' episode that brought Captains Kirk and Sisko face-to-face
item.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

When "Star Trek" celebrated its 60th anniversary in September, it was a strangely muted affair. Sure, there were fan events, screenings, and even an attempt at a world record for the biggest simultaneous Vulcan salute in history , but the lack of a "Doctor Who"-style birthday episode felt like a glaring omission. It was like everyone had shown up for the party, but the organizers had forgotten to book the headline entertainment. Luckily, there were rather more fireworks for the show's 30th birthday, when both "Voyager" and "Deep Space Nine" marked the occasion in style. "Voyager" episode "Flashback" took Tuvok (Tim Russ) back to his days on the USS Excelsior bridge alongside Original Series vets Hikaru Sulu (George Takei) and Janice Rand (Grace Lee Whitney). But it was "DS9"'s "Trials and Tribble-ations" that turned out to be the more memorable voyage to "Trek" past, as Captain Benjamin Sisko (Avery Brooks) — with the help of some then-state-of-the-art digital trickery — came face-to-face with a young Captain James T. Kirk (William Shatner). While "Flashback" aired within days of "Trek"'s September 8 birthday, fans had to wait a little longer for "DS9"'s contribution to the celebrations. Showrunner Ira Steven Behr was keen to avoid disrupting the space station-set drama's story arc for a comedic diversion, meaning that "Trials and Tribble-ations" didn't debut until November 4, 1996. In the wake of "Flashback" — not to mention Spock and Scotty's comebacks in "The Next Generation" stories "Unification" and "Relics" — the "DS9" writers' room had already decided they needed to take a very different approach. Early on, " Battlestar Galactica " creator Ronald D. Moore pitched a follow-up to Original Series episode "A Piece of the Action" (aka the one where the residents of Iotia brought 1920s gangsters to life). In an extremely meta concept that predated " Galaxy Quest " by three years, the story would have taken the Enterprise crew to a planet of Kirk and Spock impersonators. (Image credit: Paramount) "For the thirtieth anniversary, you go back, and you're basically going back to the planet of 'Star Trek' fans," Moore recalled in "The Fifty-Year Mission" by Mark A. item.title: NASA's Swift space telescope crashes back to Earth after failed rescue attempt
item.description: null NASA's Swift space telescope has reached the end of its long and winding road. Swift fell uncontrolled to Earth today (Nov. 4), 22 years after it launched but just three months after a private spacecraft was supposed to boost it to a higher, life-extending orbit. The 3,200-pound (1,450 kilograms) observatory reentered Earth's atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. EST (1239 GMT) today over northern Sumatra, according to satellite tracker Jonathan McDowell , who cited U.S. Space Force data. The fall likely didn't make much of an impact; NASA officials predicted beforehand that most of the minibus-sized Swift would burn up as it fell, and they put the odds of any of the surviving pieces hurting anyone on Earth at just 1 in 2,100. Several videos circulating on social media appear to show the spacecraft's fiery reentry, though it has yet to be independently verified. Likely reentry of @NASA's #Swift observatory over Sumatra & Malaysia at 12:39 UTC today. November 4, 2026 Likely reentry of @NASA's #Swift observatory over Sumatra & Malaysia at 12:39 UTC today. November 4, 2026 Swift — officially known as the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer — launched to Earth orbit in November 2004 on a two-year mission to study gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), the most powerful explosions in the universe . "Swift" was not an acronym but rather referred to the spacecraft's observational agility. "Swift needed to detect and locate gamma-ray bursts, communicate their position to other observatories, and then swing its telescopes around to image the burst locations before their afterglows faded out," S. Bradley Cenko, Swift's principal investigator (PI) at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, said in an Oct. 23 statement . "This typically took Swift about a minute to do." Swift didn't just observe GRBs. It also studied a variety of other cosmic bodies and phenomena, from faraway supernova explosions and feeding black holes to asteroids and comets in our own solar system. And it kept doing this long after its warranty expired — for about 20 years after, in fact. The space telescope didn't conduct its final science observation until this past Oct. 20 . (Swift underwent a name change during this stretch: In 2018, it was rechristened the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory after its first PI, who died the previous year.) "Swift delivered an incredible, lasting return on investment for the nation, designed for a two-year primary mission but productive for more than 10 times as long," Shawn Domagal-Goldman, director of NASA's Astrophysics Division, said in the same Oct. 23 statement. "In that time, Swift played a major role in advancing our understanding of the changing universe and was part of a revolution in astrophysics that showed how critical rapid-response observations are to the entire community," he added. item.title: Why the weirdest game of 2026 is also one of my favourites
item.description: Titanium Court is a bizarre world of 8-bit fairies, Shakespeare and surprise songs – its magic lies in never knowing what on earth is going on • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Earlier this year, I was stuck in hospital for several days, fuzzy on pain medication and bored out of my mind, with nothing but a Steam Deck for company. In the middle of one of those long nights, unable to sleep, I played a game called Titanium Court . It’s a strange creation that looks like it was made for the ZX Spectrum and reads like a postmodern Shakespeare adaptation – a compelling mix of strategy game and match-3 where you rearrange battlefields by matching tiles, before sending tiny lo-fi fairy armies to their deaths. At the end of this late-night run, I met a boss I’d defeated before – a comically hungry dragon – and the game asked if I would like to skip the boss fight and enjoy a musical performance instead. A game has never asked me this before. Of course, I accepted. And then, instead of the familiar tiled battlefield, I was looking at a pixellated singer-songwriter, who launched into an extremely long preamble about the mating habits of the Pacific salmon before saying, “This is a song for anyone else who ever got so horny they could die,” and launching into a soulful acoustic guitar number accompanied by crude images of leaping fish. I began to wonder if my meds were making me hallucinate. Continue reading...

item.title: “The Legacy Continues”: 2Baba Announces New Album ‘Oldest Young Man’
item.description: 2Baba wearing a hooded black pleated drape and sunglasses to announce his studio album, Oldest Young Man. Afrobeats icon 2Baba is officially returning with a full-length body of work, and November 27 is the date to mark in your calendars! The legendary singer and songwriter—formerly known as 2Face Idibia —took to Instagram to announce his upcoming studio album, titled Oldest Young Man. Taking to social media to share the exciting release date, the Afropop veteran captioned his post: The legacy continues. OLDEST YOUNG MAN drops 27.11.26. Timeless music, no expiration date. The announcement marks a huge moment for African music fans. Oldest Young Man is 2Baba’s first studio album in over six years, following his critically acclaimed 2020 project, Warriors , which featured heavyweights like Burna Boy , Wizkid , and Olamide . While he hasn’t dropped a full-length album since then, the Nigerian music pioneer has remained active with steady releases, most recently dropping singles like “ Mental ” in September 2026 and “ Ifesinachi ” earlier in the year. With over two decades at the top of the game—stretching from his days with Plantashun Boiz to solo anthems like “ African Queen “—the legend is set to prove once again why his sound stands the test of time. Oldest Young Man arrives on all streaming platforms on 27 November 2026. 2Baba posing in a draped black pleated outfit and black sunglasses ahead of his upcoming album, Oldest Young Man. *** Photo Credit: 2Baba/Instagram The post “The Legacy Continues”: 2Baba Announces New Album ‘Oldest Young Man’ appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Funke Akindele, Waje & Shoday’s London Looks Belong in Our Style Notes | See Photos
item.description: Funke Akindele, Shoday, and Waje smiling during their London promotional walk ahead of The Four UK premiere. Upon seeing these photos of Funke Akindele , Shoday and Waje , we had no choice but to pull out our notes, ready for some styling lessons. Did you see how they coordinated their looks for their London outing? Funke and Waje gave us matching buba and iro sets with colourful floral details, while Shoday arrived with a custom embroidered blazer that made its own case for a place in our style notes. The trio were in the UK for the promotional campaign of The Four: No One Fights Alone , and the outing came with another exciting update. Funke Akindele Network and FilmOne Entertainment have announced that the film will have its UK premiere on 29 November at ODEON Luxe Leicester Square in London, ahead of its worldwide cinema release on 11 December. Now, if you’re wondering how Funke and Waje managed to wear matching outfits without looking identical, the answer is in the details. Both looks started with off-white textured cotton, but the floral appliqués gave each one a distinct finish. Funke’s outfit features crimson-red roses with spiral stitching across the bodice and bell sleeves, while yellow sunflowers and leafy green stems run down her wrapper. She completed the look with a golden-yellow head wrap, layered gold necklaces, a broad cuff bracelet and metallic red platform sandals. Funke Akindele Buba and Iro Outfit for The Four London Promo Waje went for lavender roses across the neckline and sleeves of her blouse, with large green floral appliqués decorating the hem of her wrapper. She kept the colour story going with a matching lavender-trimmed scarf, a gold necklace accented with turquoise stones, coordinating earrings and multi-coloured platform heels. Same base colour, different floral story. We love that. Waje outdoors in London promoting The Four: No One Fights Alone in a lavender floral buba and iro set. And Shoday? He clearly had no plans to be the odd one out. His single-breasted blazer featured bold chevron embroidery in turquoise, yellow, red and blue, worn over a beige mesh-knit top and cream wide-leg trousers. Stacked silver Cuban-link chains and dark dress shoes completed the look, giving the colourful jacket room to do its thing. Shoday in a custom geometric chevron-embroidered blazer during The Four promotional tour in London. With the fashion notes taken, we’re also looking forward to seeing what the cast has in store for the London premiere. The Four: No One Fights Alone features Funke Akindele, Waje, Chioma Akpotha, Bisola Aiyeola, Richard Mofe-Damijo, Lateef Adedimeji, Timini Egbuson and Uzor Arukwe, among others. The film premieres at ODEON Luxe Leicester Square on 29 November before its global cinema release on 11 December. item.title: Ejiro Amos Tafiri Unveils REVERIE, Its Spring/Summer 2027 Collection, Celebrating Reinvention in African Luxury
item.description: Ejiro Amos Tafiri , a Pan-African luxury fashion house founded in Lagos in 2010, has unveiled REVERIE, its Spring/Summer 2027 (SS27) collection, at an exclusive private showcase in Lagos on Sunday, October 25, 2026, held alongside Lagos Fashion Week. The showcase brought together distinguished guests, fashion industry leaders, patrons and representatives of the British Council Nigeria, including chef and media personality Hilda Baci, for a presentation of the house’s latest collection. REVERIE explores renewal and reinvention through contemporary African luxury. Bringing together expressive silhouettes, intricate craftsmanship and a refined colour palette, the collection presents a visual statement that celebrates the evolving language of African fashion. Through considered design and craftsmanship, REVERIE reflects the house’s continued exploration of contemporary African aesthetics, presenting pieces that balance creative expression with the distinctive design sensibility for which Ejiro Amos Tafiri is known. Founded by designer Ejiro Amos Tafiri, known for her signature Drapes, the fashion house has spent 16 years developing a distinctive identity within the luxury fashion landscape. Its design language is characterized by expressive drapery, fluid tailoring and the thoughtful use of indigenous textiles, bringing African craftsmanship into contemporary fashion. The Lagos unveiling followed the third edition of Fashioning a Legacy: Leaving a Mark in Time, held on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the British Council in Ikoyi, Lagos. The conference brought together designers, stylists, retail professionals and emerging creatives to discuss building sustainable careers and creating lasting impact within the fashion industry. Together, the events reflect Ejiro Amos Tafiri’s continued engagement with the broader creative ecosystem, connecting fashion, education, craftsmanship and the development of emerging talent. The REVERIE presentation forms part of the house’s 16-year milestone and will be followed by an exclusive showcase in Abuja on November 21, 2026. The forthcoming event will bring together members of the diplomatic community, government officials, fashion patrons and invited guests for a further presentation of the house’s work. As Ejiro Amos Tafiri looks towards its next chapter, REVERIE embodies an ongoing exploration of renewal and reinvention, reinforcing the house’s commitment to advancing contemporary African luxury through expressive design and intricate craftsmanship. item.title: Pan-African School Games 2026: Celebrating Young Talent, School Pride and New Opportunities
item.description: The Pan-African School Games 2026 brought together young athletes from schools across Lagos for three days of swimming, athletics and football, celebrating sporting talent, school pride and the opportunities that organized competition can create for children and young people. Held at James Hope College, Lekki, from 16 to 18 October, the second edition of the Games featured the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. Students competed for individual honours and school points while gaining valuable experience in a structured, multi-sport environment. The competition also welcomed sporting stakeholders and scouts, reinforcing the wider ambition of the Pan-African School Games: to give young athletes a platform where their abilities can be demonstrated, recognized and developed. Building on the Inaugural Games The second edition of the Pan-African School Games built on the foundation established by the inaugural Games in 2025, continuing the vision of creating meaningful sporting opportunities for young athletes. The 2026 edition welcomed schools and student-athletes for three days of swimming, athletics and football, providing a platform for competition, talent development and school pride. Beyond the sporting results, the Games continued to advance a broader ambition: to connect schools, athletes, sporting stakeholders and educational institutions while creating opportunities for young people to develop their abilities and explore future pathways through sport. Day One: Swimming Opens the Games Swimming opened the competition, bringing young swimmers together for races across the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. The opening day set the pace for the Games as athletes took to the pool to test their abilities, pursue strong performances and earn points for their schools. The races highlighted the preparation, discipline and technique required to compete, while providing young swimmers with valuable experience in a formal sporting environment. For many of the students, the opportunity to compete alongside athletes from other schools added to the significance of the experience. Each race contributed to the overall competition, with schools beginning their campaigns for medals and category honours. Day Two: Athletics Puts Young Athletes to the Test Athletics took centre stage on the second day, with track and field events testing the speed, strength, coordination and technique of the young competitors. Athletes competed in running, jumping and throwing events, earning points for their schools as the standings developed. Each discipline presented a different challenge, giving students opportunities to demonstrate their abilities and compete for individual and team honours. The athletics programme added another dimension to the Games, highlighting the variety of talent within the participating schools and the value of giving young athletes opportunities to develop through competition. item.title: Afrique Femme & CANEX WKND 2026 Partner to Celebrate Francophone Fashion, Culture, and Female Leadership in Lagos
item.description: From November 5 to 8, 2026 , Lagos will become the epicenter of African creativity as Afrique Femme brings the 6th edition of the Brunch des AfricanWoman2.0 to CANEX WKND 2026 at the iconic Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture & Creative Arts. Organized by Afreximbank in collaboration with the African Union and the AfCFTA Secretariat, Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX WKND) is Africa’s premier event celebrating the continent’s creative and cultural industries. Under the overarching theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World: From FESTAC ’77 to CANEX ’27,” this year’s gathering will connect thousands of creative entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers, and cultural icons from across Global Africa and the diaspora. Spotlighting Francophone Luxury & Made-in-Africa Fashion As part of this landmark event, Afrique Femme is hosting a dedicated Exhibition Pavilion designed to bridge Francophone and Anglophone creative ecosystems. The pavilion will feature curated showcases, pop-ups, and private sales from leading West and Central African designers. Attendees will experience exclusive collections from celebrated brands including Makeda by AYA Konan ,, KUMI , KWELAKU , and Galipette Atelier , highlighting the richness, craftsmanship, and global potential of Francophone fashion. The African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch A core highlight of the week will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026 , with the African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch . Bringing together 200 to 250 influential women leaders, policymakers, innovators, and international dignitaries, the high-level gathering will feature keynote addresses, strategic panels, and structured B2B networking aimed at fostering female leadership and economic empowerment across the continent. “We are thrilled to bring the African Woman 2.0 platform to Lagos alongside CANEX WKND 2026,” said Aïssata Sidibé N’DIA , Managing Director of RED Côte d’Ivoire / Afrique Femme. “This partnership offers an extraordinary opportunity to celebrate the ingenuity of African creative entrepreneurs, showcase Francophone fashion excellence on a global stage, and build lasting cross-border trade and investment synergies across Africa.” Event & Registration Details Dates: November 5–8, 2026 Venue: Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture & Creative Arts (National Theatre), Lagos, Nigeria Registration: Delegate attendance at CANEX WKND 2026 is 100% free , but pre-registration is mandatory. Visitors are invited to register at wknd.canex.africa , select “Visitor / Delegate,” and indicate “Afrique Femme” under referral source. About Afrique Femme AfriqueFemme.com is a leading Pan-African digital media platform produced by Weblogy Group. Dedicated to inspiring, educating, and empowering African women, Afrique Femme reaches millions of readers and viewers monthly across West Africa and the global diaspora through high-impact editorial content, TV shows, and flagship events such as the Week-end des African Woman 2.0 . item.title: African Philanthropy Leaders Call for Bolder, Locally Led Giving at the 2026 APF Conference in Cape Town
item.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. The conference opened on Sunday evening with a reception at Cape Point Vineyards, where Executive Director Mosun Layode welcomed delegates, members and acknowledged APF Board members, including Chair Gbenga Oyebode , Wale Adeosun , and Nyimpini Mabunda . Former Board Member Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa urged guests to look past the continent’s challenges and toward its potential and to use the days ahead to turn conversations into partnerships. It was an evening of connection before two days of ideas at the Norval Foundation. Reimagining the Future Monday, 26 October, began with a call to build bridges across regions, languages, and funding silos. Mosun Layode and Gbenga Oyebode officially opened and welcomed all delegates to the conference. Dr. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka , former Vice President of South Africa, spoke of education as a sacred right of every African child and of bringing young people into decision-making. In the first keynote, Gary Lubner, Founder of the This Day Foundation, described giving away 95 percent of his wealth during his lifetime and said it was easier and more joyful than holding it for heirs. Old money thinking, he argued, is a major barrier to giving, and generosity includes time and effort as well as cash. The numbers framed the challenge. Delegates heard that Africa needs about $1.3 trillion in financing each year, while philanthropy contributes $5 billion to $6 billion. The task is to use that small pool to unlock far larger sources, such as pension funds and fixed-income assets, so money reaches businesses that create jobs. In an afternoon keynote moderated by Marlene Ogawa of Synergos, Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa , South Africa CEO of Naspers, and Gareth Ackerman, Non-Executive Director at Pick n Pay, kept things practical: back women entrepreneurs without taking equity, start with your own family and community, use local distributors, and make it easier to travel between African countries. One retraining program they discussed moved 7,200 of 8,000 university graduates into tech jobs. The difference between charity and philanthropy, they said, is helping people help themselves. The day also asked hard questions about who belongs. A panel on migration, moderated by Dr Ndidi Okonkw

item.title: Pepsi Agba Baller Promo: A Winner Every Minute with ₦800 Million in Cash Prizes
item.description: The Pepsi Agba Baller Promo by Seven-Up Bottling Company (SBC) has launched with over 720 winners, including 4 millionaires, emerging in the first live draws for the ₦800 million reward pool across selected participating regions. The promotion officially commenced on October 28, 2026 and began its live prize draws on November 2, giving eligible consumers the opportunity to win cash prizes while enjoying their favourite SBC beverages. The promotion is running across Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara, Osun, Ekiti, Kogi, Niger and Ondo states offering consumers an opportunity to win everyday until January 3, 2027. With ₦800 million in total rewards, the Pepsi Agba Baller promo features a winner every minute from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. daily, four ₦1 million winners every day, and a ₦10 million mega jackpot winner every Sunday. The first set of winners includes Oluwatoyin , Oreofe and Damilola from Lagos, and Adeniyi from Ogun State, who each won ₦1 million on the opening day of the draws. Speaking on the promotion , Yewande Ade-Alao , Marketing Manager at SBC, said, “At Seven-Up Bottling Company, we are always looking for ways to make our consumers’ experiences more rewarding. With the Pepsi Agba Baller Promo, consumers can win cash prizes while enjoying the beverages they love. We are excited to see consumers already winning, and we look forward to rewarding many more participants in the promotion.” The Pepsi Agba Baller Promo adds excitement to the festive season, rewarding consumer loyalty and giving eligible consumers a reason to look out for the distinctive yellow covers on Pepsi, 7UP, Mirinda, Teem and other Seven-Up Bottling Company products. To participate, consumers need to purchase eligible products from SBC with the yellow cover to get the unique code printed underneath. Participants can then enter the draw by dialing or scanning the QR code on the bottles and promotional materials for a chance to win a share of the ₦800 million prize pool. Consumers can check the winners’ list and verify their winnings on the official campaign website . To ensure consumer protection, winners are contacted through the designated promotion number, 0700 134 1104, and will receive a confirmation SMS. For additional assistance or enquiries, please contact Seven-Up Bottling Company’s dedicated consumer support lines: 0805 690 0900 and 0806 690 0900. Follow @PepsiNaija and @sbc_nigeria across all social media platforms for live updates and winner announcements. About Seven-Up Bottling Company Seven-Up Bottling Company Ltd (SBC) is one of Nigeria’s leading beverage manufacturing and distribution companies. Since 1960, SBC has grown into a household name with a portfolio of iconic brands including Pepsi, 7UP, Mirinda, Mountain Dew, Teem, Supa Komando, Lipton Ice Tea and Aquafina Premium Drinking Water, SBC continues to drive innovation, create value and contribute to Nigeria’s development. item.title: AI & Equity: The Big Conversations at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026
item.description: The Goalkeepers 2026 Event in Dakar brought together innovators, global leaders and experts on how AI can be further leveraged by Africans for an equitable future On October 29, 2026, Africans gathered in Dakar, Senegal, to discuss the continent’s relationship with the world’s fastest-growing technology: artificial intelligence (AI). This event was part of the Goalkeepers 2026 series and was themed “Make This Matter: Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth .” It brought together professionals and innovators who focused on how Africa can adopt AI to fill gaps and ensure equitable access across various sectors . Africans are leveraging AI for business, education and more, but as AI continues to develop and expand rapidly, it is crucial for us to use it on a bigger scale, ensuring collective development and an equitable future for all. This makes the Goalkeepers 2026 event in Dakar particularly significant. Nigerian influencer, Saskay, at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026 The event included several activities, including performances from the legendary Youssou N’Dour , a Qui veut changer le monden session where people pitched their ideas, conversations about AI and equity and more. Here are some of the major talking points at the event: AI and Existing Solutions The event was graciously hosted in English and French by Fatou Jupiter Toure , who opened by sharing a powerful African message: “It is not about what you can do. It is about what we can do for each other.” Despite the diverse cultures and beliefs that exist on the continent, Africans have remained held by the belief of “I am because you are.” This is why, despite AI’s fast growth, Africans are coming together to examine how much it concerns them, how it can be properly leveraged and what dangers and challenges lie ahead. Fatou Jupiter Toure hosting the Goalkeepers 2026 event in Dakar Nevertheless, Africans have done a great deal of work with AI. Innovators have used AI tools to provide solutions in their local communities. Vyonne Njeri shared how she got into healthcare and how AI has been greatly helping in the community she serves. In the Goalkeepers 2026 Report , Vyonne said she got into healthcare during a visit to see her uncle, a priest in a small, East Kenyan town called Modogashe. She highlighted that even though AI greatly supports her work, she remains the clinical officer. She explained that “AI is not perfect. It must not take over clinical work. But it can help us share across accessible healthcare. It can help discover what could have been missed early. We still need people to be trained, but AI tools can greatly support us.” Like Vyonne, Mamadou Ly also shared why and how AI can aid learning, especially in local languages. He said, “Education is not just about reading and writing. It is also an act of dignity.” Mamadou Ly at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026. item.title: Tanqueray No. TEN Curates a Citrus-Led Cocktail Journey at Moonshot 2026
item.description: At Moonshot 2026 , where some of Africa’s brightest minds gathered to exchange ideas, build meaningful connections, and shape the future, Tanqueray No. TEN brought a refreshing cocktail experience that complemented the energy and spirit of the event. Situated at the heart of Moonshot, the Tanqueray No. TEN bar served as a vibrant hub where inspiring conversations and exceptional cocktails came together. While attendees engaged in thought-provoking discussions and explored new ideas, Tanqueray No. TEN created a space to pause, connect, and enjoy expertly crafted serves built around the gin’s distinctive citrus character. Throughout the event, guests experienced the versatility of Tanqueray No. TEN through a carefully curated selection of serves, from the timeless Tanqueray & Tonic to refreshing flavour combinations featuring grapefruit, strawberry, rosemary, mint, orange peels, and other fresh botanicals. Each serve was designed to highlight the bright, citrus-forward profile that has made Tanqueray No. TEN a globally celebrated gin. Whether drawn to the zesty notes of grapefruit, the sweetness of strawberry, the freshness of mint, the complexity of rosemary, or the vibrancy of orange peels, attendees embarked on a flavourful journey that showcased the craftsmanship at the heart of every bottle of Tanqueray No. TEN. As day transitioned into evening, the atmosphere evolved into one of celebration and connection. Guests gathered around the Tanqueray No. TEN bar, where great cocktails became a natural catalyst for conversation, helping spark new connections and memorable moments throughout the event. This flavour-led experience resonated strongly with the spirit of Moonshot itself. Just as the event celebrates individuals who challenge convention, embrace creativity, and reimagine what’s possible, Tanqueray No. TEN invited guests to explore new flavour combinations and discover the versatility of a gin crafted for those who appreciate exceptional taste and quality. As Moonshot 2026 came to a close, attendees left with fresh inspiration and unforgettable memories. Among them were the flavours, conversations, and experiences shared over a glass of Tanqueray No. TEN, proving once again that every bold idea deserves an exceptional serve. Here’s to bold ideas, meaningful connections, and raising a glass of Tanqueray No. TEN to the moments that bring people together. Drink Responsibly. Not for persons under the legal purchase age. item.title: LagosFashionWeek2026: Personal Style Is Alive and Well – Just Ask Ifeoma Odogwu
item.description: From runway shows to intimate presentations and the week’s most stylish gatherings, the fashion editor and creative consultant made a case for directional dressing with oodles of personality. Ifeoma Odogwu , better known as Hyperfashun , is easily one of the best dressed women in Lagos, and arguably on the continent and per usual her Lagos Fashion Week style is peerless. A familiar face in Nigeria’s fashion industry, the former Genevieve Magazine fashion editor, stylist to stars such as Toke Makinwa and more, the creative consultant has spent years working with designers, discovering emerging talent and helping shape the visual language of Nigerian fashion. So, naturally, when Lagos Fashion Week comes around, we’re just as interested in what she’s wearing as we are in what she’s watching. From the bustling Lagos Fashion Week tents at Federal Palace Hotel to a packed calendar of offsite presentations and fashion events across the city, Odogwu embraced the occasion with a wardrobe that made getting dressed part of the experience. At the tents, she joined the fashion crowd for presentations by Y’Wande , NYA The Label , E.S.O by Liman and FIA Factory , taking in some of the exciting design talent shaping the season. But as anyone familiar with Lagos Fashion Week knows, the shows have evolved. Some of the week’s most interesting moments happen elsewhere, and Odogwu’s itinerary reflected just how much the city’s fashion calendar has expanded. She made the rounds at presentations by Jewel Jemila , The Ladymaker, Rendoll, Kilentar, Onalaja and Orange Culture , and made time for the social side of fashion week, too, including the Made By Us pop-up at Melrose Loft and Tiffany Amber’s Breakfast Club. What makes Odogwu particularly interesting to watch is the perspective she brings to personal style. As someone whose career has been built around fashion imagery, designers and creative expression, her wardrobe offers another way of engaging with the industry she’s helped champion. Ifeoma has a certain clarity in her style and an unmatched point of view, something that’s often lacking in the sameness of our Instagram-driven world. Her style reminds us that what makes personal style compelling is individuality, curiosity and a willingness to have fun with fashion. Scroll through for a closer look at Ifeoma Odogwu’s Lagos Fashion Week wardrobe, from the runway tents to the events around town. Ifeoma Odogwu/Instagram Romantic vibes in @jeweljemila . Happy to be back in Lagos for another exciting season of @lagosfashionweekofficial . Day 1 of prancing around included the Jewel Jemilia anniversary show, then made a dash before the doors at @atafo__ closed, then to @ejiroamostafiri and finally ended at the official Heineken and Lagos fashion week press cocktail. Phew! And we are only just getting started!! item.title: For the Girls, For Our Health: The Active Circle x Zephans & Co. Celebrate Breast Cancer Awareness Month With The Girls’ Club
item.description: Breast Cancer Awareness Month ended on the most vibrant, empowering note in Lagos! The Active Circle , powered by contemporary fashion brand Zephans & Co. , brought together fabulous women from all walks of life for The Girls’ Club – a dreamy, pink-hued wellness wonderland created to celebrate womanhood while championing critical conversations around breast health. The morning kicked off on a high-energy note with a beginner-friendly Pilates session led by top instructor Dammy Olufowobi , proving that movement can be both joyful and deeply rewarding. Adhering to the chic Pretty in Pink dress code, attendees transformed the studio into an editorial runway of blush and beauty. Beyond the movement and aesthetic moments, the heart of the event was an intimate “Breast Talk” session delivered by Dr. Omolola Salako – widely known as The People’s Oncologist . Dr. Salako unpacked the importance of early detection, self-examinations, and practical steps for proactive health, making the conversation feel personal, approachable, and empowering. Chisom Okuguni, Convener of The Active Circle, shared that the initiative was designed to equip women with the knowledge and community support needed to prioritize their well-being every single day. The wellness morning provided an opportunity for the ladies to interact and share experiences, connect on a deeper level, all while learning to care for their breast health. Proudly supported by BellaNaija , The Girls’ Club proved that when women come together for movement, health, and community, magic happens. item.title: How the New Tax Stamp Could Show Up in Everyday Life
item.description: We’ve all been there: planning a weekend dinner with friends, throwing a birthday bash, or just kicking back at home with a few favourite treats. Drinks and refreshments are basically a staple of these moments. But have you ever stopped to think about how behind-the-scenes government policies end up changing the price tags on those items? With the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) rolling out its new excise stamp policy in January 2026, that question is at the forefront, especially for brands that make things like alcohol, tobacco, and sugar-sweetened beverages. Honestly, nobody’s really stressing over the policy itself. What people care about is the ripple effect: how companies handle the new regulation and whether those adjustments will make our favourite items more expensive on the shelf. When Business Meets Your Wallet Behind every product is a mountain of decisions from packaging and distribution to compliance and production. Most of the time, we never see this happening, but it plays a huge role in how items are priced. When new regulations bring extra costs, companies find themselves at a crossroads. Some choose to absorb the blow internally to keep customers happy, while others might tweak their prices. It really comes down to the specific brand, the market, and how heavy the financial lift is. For everyday shoppers, that’s usually the moment a boring policy talk suddenly feels very real. What Does This Mean for How We Spend ? The change probably won’t hit overnight, and it might not even be dramatic. But over time, small shifts in everyday prices can change how we shop. You might find yourself comparing brands a bit more closely, hunting for promos and discounts, or rethinking how much cash you drop on certain treats. Brands, meanwhile, are caught in a tricky balancing act: keeping loyal customers without going broke on rising operating costs. Just keep in mind: a new tax stamp doesn’t automatically mean prices are shooting up. It all depends on how companies adapt and whether those extra costs trickle down to us. The Bigger Picture At the end of the day, this is really about finding a middle ground. The government wants solid systems to collect taxes, while businesses need a framework that lets them stay afloat and grow. But come to think of it, the authorities are already equipped with internal tracking solutions, such as electronic invoicing from FIRS alongside the Customs Service’s B’Odogwu digital excise register, rendering physical paper tags largely redundant. Striking that balance matters because business decisions don’t just stay on a spreadsheet. They shape the things we buy, the choices we make, and how we manage our money. Right now, it’s still a bit early to tell what the full impact on consumers will be. But staying clued in on what’s driving the market makes it a whole lot easier to navigate the changes coming our way. item.title: BN Prose: A Beachside Conversation Amara Nnaji
item.description: Generated Image “Eiss Hanty, why are you sitting on the beach sand playing with shingles?” “How is that your business now, Madam Lantana?” I responded. “Ah, I care for you na.” “Sorry oo. Madam-carer, just let me be,” I grunted, picking up pebbles and tossing them back into the water. “No, seriously, I care about you. You left home claiming to go to your Alternative Therapist, yet look at you sitting by the beach playing with sand like a kindergartener,” Lantana said. “Lantana, please, do you mind? I really need my space right now.” “Abeg shift joor! Aunty lone-ranger. Every time you need your space, you need your space; you no dey tire of yourself?” “No, ma. I am still my best company.” “Very boring. How a human being can stay alone and claim that they are having fun by themself baffles me.” Lantana sits beside me and nudges closer. I side-eye her and shift aside. She moves closer. I sidle away; she comes closer and drapes her right leg across mine with a twinkle in her eyes. “Babe, free me na. I came here to breathe.” I begged. “You came here to breathe? Egbami, you been dey suffocate before? You left home to go to Iwona’s for therapy, so how did you now end up at the beach? “She say she get another customer.” I picked up a smooth pebble and a coral and lay back on the sand. “I no understand. She get another customer bi bawo? Didn’t you book this slot?” “I did.” “So, which kain talk be that?” Lantana was bristling already. “I was running late and sent her a message.” “You were running late? You ran from your house to here across three postcodes? With which strength abi you wan kpai?” Lantana looked worried. “Gaskiya, Lantana, you no get sense. Run as in how na? Shey today na Parkrun ni? I say I come late.” “Aha! That is what you should say na, auntie. You know you runners, once you say run, we take it literally.” “So, I go run the 22 miles because I want to prove what?” I glared at her. “Ah, a le so! We never can tell with weirdos like you.” She shot me a sly grin. “Lantana, I can’t deal right now. Just free me; let me breathe.” “So you came late? How many minutes late?” “26 minutes.” “Haba, that is so unlike you. What happened?” “I tried to catch the 3:15 bus but missed it. Then walked 15 minutes to the next bus stop, and the bus was delayed for 10 minutes. I decided to walk to the next one so I could catch a direct bus to her place, but that bus stop was closed. I went to the next one.” “Johnny Walka. Why didn’t you simply take a cab? See as you punish yourself on top £20.” “I no bi God na. I no see say na so e go bẹ.” I stood up, stretched and began walking into the waters. “Babe, you wan jump inside water? No koba mẹ o,” she screeched. “Olódò ni e. Jump say wetin happen? Say she save money wey I for pay the therapist?” “Wow, that is awesome. Look how you reframed it already. item.title: Who Checks on the Person Everyone Calls?
item.description: At 11:47 p.m., the family WhatsApp group suddenly comes alive. “Good evening, fam. Please, we have an emergency.” Before the second message arrives, everyone already knows who will be tagged. The eldest daughter who always knows what to do. The brother with the most stable job. The aunty abroad. The uncle in Lagos who “knows somebody.” The cousin with a car. The friend who always picks up, even at an unreasonable hour. In many Nigerian families, care has a name and a phone number. It belongs to the person who pays the unexpected bill, makes the difficult call, accompanies someone to the hospital, settles the family disagreement, or says, “Don’t worry, I’ll handle it.” We call them strong. Responsible. Dependable. We praise their shoulders without asking if they hurt. This is the human question at the heart of AXA Mansard’ s Culture of Care campaign: “ Who cares for the person everyone calls”? The Person Who Always Finds a Way Every family, friendship circle and workplace has one. Sometimes, she is the firstborn daughter who became a second mother long before she was ready. She remembers birthdays, school fees, hospital appointments, and the details everyone else forgets. Sometimes, he is the brother whose first good job quietly turned him into the family’s emergency fund and dependable source. His salary has not grown significantly, but the number of people depending on it has. Other times, it is the mom who serves everyone’s food before sitting down to eat. The father who never admits that he is worried. The friend who listens to everyone’s problems but rarely talks about her own. The colleague who carries the team whenever someone falls behind. These people are often so good at caring that we stop seeing the effort involved. We see the transfer alert, but not the personal plan they postponed. We see the paid bills, but not the hours spent calling doctors, arranging transport, and sitting beside a bed. We see the calm voice saying, “Everything will be fine,” but not the fear or uncertainty behind it. That person everyone calls may also be tired. They may worry about money, struggle with their health, or quietly wonder who would come through for them if they could no longer carry everyone else. Care Has More Than One Currency In Nigeria, many conversations about family responsibility often begin and end with money. Who paid the school fees? Who sent money home? Who handled the rent? Who covered the medical emergency? These questions matter, especially as the cost of living continues to stretch households. But money is only one currency of care. Care can also be time ! The sitting in traffic to pick up someone else’s child; the night spent at the hospital bedside; the regular reminder to an elderly parent to remember their medication. Or listening to the same worry repeatedly because the person telling you has nowhere else to take it. Care can be access ! Advice. Attention. Prayer. Food. Transport. Encouragement. A job referral. item.title: Meet Mo Odukoya: Pastor Jimmy Introduces His Wife to The Fountain of Life Church
item.description: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and Pastor Mo Odukoya pose together following their formal church introduction If you’re a member of The Fountain of Life Church and you were at yesterday’s service, we’re a little jealous. What do you mean you got to witness Pastor Jimmy Odukoya introduce his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel , to the congregation in person? Yes, right there at the church’s headquarters in Ilupeju, Lagos, the senior pastor had a special person to introduce, and he made sure everyone knew exactly who she was. As she joined him at the altar, he introduced her as Pastor Mo Odukoya , the church’s new first lady, and the congregation welcomed the couple with cheers and applause. Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel, holding hands during their official introduction at The Fountain of Life Church But before that introduction, Pastor Jimmy had a little story to tell. He spoke about how he had been navigating life alone since becoming the church’s senior pastor, and how he had been searching for someone to share the journey with. He invited Mo to join him, and the two walked up to the altar together, marking the moment with a warm reception from the congregation. Pastor Jimmy Odukoya introduces his wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel, on stage at The Fountain of Life Church in Ilupeju, Lagos For those who know Pastor Jimmy beyond the pulpit, there’s quite a bit to his story. He took over as senior pastor of The Fountain of Life Church in 2023, following the passing of his father, the late Pastor Taiwo Odukoya , who co-founded the ministry with his wife, Pastor Bimbo Odukoya . He is also an actor and musician, and film audiences may recognise him as Oba Ade in the 2022 historical film The Woman King, where he starred alongside Viola Davis . Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and Mo Jasmine Daniel after announcing their marriage to the congregation And now, there’s a new chapter to this story with Mo. Introduced to the congregation as Pastor Mo Odukoya, she is the daughter of Reverend Theophilus and Bolaji Daniel . She also took a moment to address the church, expressing her pleasure and honour at joining the ministry family. The couple also made sure their outfits were in sync for the occasion. Pastor Jimmy wore a structured burnt-orange native outfit with dark detailing on the cuffs and a matching necklace, while Pastor Mo chose a long-sleeved, floor-length dress in orange and copper patterns, finished with a matching clutch and accessories.
